items.title: feat(dd043): PR-3 — basquin-maven-injector, instrumentation with zero edits to the target's source

labels.name: approved-awaiting-merge
labels.description: Approver agent approved; waiting for human merge

items.body:
DD-043 PR-3. A Maven **core extension** that adds Basquin's Quarkus extension to a target application's build via `-Dmaven.ext.class.path`, with **zero edits to any file in that application's tree**. Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-26-dd043-pr3-maven-injector.md` (8 tasks, all reviewed).

**390 tests, 0 failures**, and `scripts/verify-dd043-pr3.sh` reports **27 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** (`bench-results/verify-20260730T215842Z/RESULTS.md`, stamped `b980e1f`, produced *after* its commit against a clean tree so the stamp and the content agree). Every count here is derived from that run, not typed.

`scripts/check-citations.py` checks that derivation in CI. Its output is captured as a committed artifact — `bench-results/citations-20260730T214700Z/output.txt` — because a live total cited only to the script computing it can never verify, and this figure was retyped three times chasing the tool. That run: 1689 parsed, 1241 verified, 299 UNCHECKED, 136 allowlisted, 2 reported, 13 disclosed absences, 0 failed. The sum is asserted against the parsed total, so nothing falls through silently. **Those are "before" figures and HEAD does not reproduce them**: the artifact was captured at `086fafc` against a dirty tree, deliberately, because it is the evidence for the 2 reported values this PR then fixed. Its README and `TODO.md` both say so; this line did not, which is round 12's second finding. `0 failed` is the part that holds at both commits, and it is the part CI re-checks on every push — for today's real figures run `python3 scripts/check-citations.py` and read its own disposition line rather than quoting any number above. An earlier version of this line read "1,174 verified, 265 UNCHECKED" and omitted two of the four remaining buckets, so it did not add up — round 11's finding 5, and precisely the partial-accounting shape this tool exists to catch. It catches dead paths, values quoted beside a citation the cited file does not contain, and line citations past end-of-file. **It does not catch a `file:N` repointed to a wrong-but-existing line** outside the two pinned `citations.txt` files. An earlier version of this line said "1211 citations checked" and "fails CI on a stale line" — both were wider than the check, which is round 10's finding 7.

Rounds 6 and 7 each inserted a row mid-table and each invalidated a batch of line citations. Round 8's insertion invalidated **none** — citations are now anchored by row key, heading or bare path, so only three line-numbered references remained and all three still resolved. The churn was never inherent to the work; it came from citing a *position* in a file instead of a *name* in it.

This body has been stale eight times — 374/"three guards", 380/"four guards", 382/"five shapes", a "one shape" claim a later guard falsified, a superseded run pointer, a "never executed" disclosure false for three rounds, a "two shapes the banner cannot detect" count that is four, and a "~354 lines" spec-doc figure that was 387 for the last five commits (round 12's finding 1 — now deleted rather than retyped, since a figure that cannot drift beats one that is currently right). Treat anything here as something to check against the run directory, not to quote.

## Acceptance — §5.2's two-artifact bar, both halves passed

| Half | Target | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| JVM | **`rest-villains`** (a real third-party app) | banner lists `basquin`; boundary poll returned `787,-684,9\|0\|\|`, not `miss` | `bench-results/dd043-pr3-restvillains-2026-07-26/` |
| Native | Phase-0 fixture | `Installed features: [basquin, cdi, rest, smallrye-context-propagation, vertx]` | `bench-results/dd043-pr3-native-2026-07-26/` |

PR-2 reached its banner via a **manual pom edit** and its README handed PR-3 the job of doing it with none. That patch was reverted first; `pristine-proof.txt` carries the check-5 evidence, including the build-log argument that `rest-villains/pom.xml` carried no Basquin declaration at the moment Maven read the model (`already declares` appears 0 times while the injector line is present, which proves the else-branch was taken — `pristine-proof.txt` explicitly **retracted** the stronger claim that the `instrumented` line prints only in that case; it prints unconditionally, `BasquinInjector.java:108-109`). That is narrower than the "clean during the build" claim this line used to make, and it is what the artifact actually establishes.

**The unconfounded piece** is `basquin-quarkus-deployment`: no pom anywhere names it, so the bootstrap resolver fetching it can only be explained by the injected repository reaching it. Both runs purged `com/basquin` from the local repo first with absence proofs.

## Two things that would have shipped a silent no-op

**The repository injection is two-level.** A `Repository` on the `Model` **alone is a no-op** at `afterProjectsRead`. `setRemoteArtifactRepositories(...)` is what refreshes the list Maven and quarkus-maven-plugin consume. Measured by spike S5 (`bench-results/dd043-s5-repo-injection-2026-07-26/`); §5 now states it, because the model-only form is what the old text implied and it fails silently.

**The Sisu index.** Maven discovers core extensions through `META-INF/sisu/javax.inject.Named`, not by scanning `@Named`; Gradle does not generate it. Without it the jar builds, all tests pass, and Maven never loads the participant. Now enforced by a Gradle task `finalizedBy('jar')` — not merely `check`, since the release path publishes without running `check`.

## Guards — eight silent-bypass shapes closed

Four guard methods — `failOnConflictingManagedVersion`, `failOnUnusableDeclaration`, `failOnConflictingDeclaredVersion`, `failOnUnusableSiblingDeclaration` — carrying **seven `throw MavenExecutionException` sites** that close **eight shapes** (`failOnUnusableDeclaration`'s single throw bundles four), behind **eight mutation checks** — one per throw site plus `skip` for the operator opt-out, each asserting *which named test* fails when that specific branch is neutered, each clearing `test-results` first so no row can pass off the previous mutation's XML.

Two of the seven shapes were found only in round 4, by **measuring** Maven's resolution rather than reasoning about it: a declared `com.basquin:basquin-core` — the injected artifact's *sibling*, which every earlier guard ignored — at a conflicting version, or at `test`/`provided` scope, produced a green build carrying the wrong core. Measurement: `bench-results/dd043-pr3-r4-guard-measurement-2026-07-29/` (14 poms, 17 build logs, real Maven 3.9.15):

1. `-Dbasquin.inject.skip`
2. a conflicting `dependencyManagement` pin
3. a conflicting **declared** version
4. an **unusable declaration** — wrong scope, non-`jar` type, a classifier, or `<exclusions>`

Guard 4 accumulated four shapes, each found only after the previous was fixed, so it is written as a **whitelist** of what is usable rather than a list of known-bad values. **Four shapes — declared `<exclusions>`, managed `<exclusions>`, a managed sibling `<scope>` and a declared sibling `<scope>` — are what §5.2's banner acceptance cannot detect** (`docs/ROADMAP.md` and `docs/THIRD-PARTY-APPS.md` each enumerate all four): the extension still appears in `Installed features` while a stripped `basquin-core` leaves it unusable. The managed one arrived in `a61a90c` and falsified the "one shape" wording in five places at once; all are now corrected.

## Also in scope

- **`ci.yml`'s path filters never listed `basquin-quarkus/**`** — a change confined to the extension ran **no CI at all**. #102 was green only incidentally.
- The Pages Maven repo now carries all four artifacts; `deploymentArtifact`'s version is derived, not typed twice.
- `basquin-init.gradle`, the Gradle counterpart — implements **only** `-Dbasquin.inject.skip`. None of the four guard methods above exist on the Gradle path, so a Gradle target gets **no silent-bypass protection at all**. This is a disclosed gap, not an untested one; the Maven path is what PR-3 claims.
- `scripts/verify-dd043-pr3.sh` — five sequential stages writing a timestamped `RESULTS.md` whose every figure is derived. Its `assert_absent` helper requires a **sentinel** so an absence claim cannot pass on a log that was never written.
- §8.1 **resolved**: Apicurio's *server* has no native build on the 3.x line. Evidence tracked at `bench-results/dd043-apicurio-native-2026-07-26/`. A **new row-5 gate** recorded: the Quarkus version range over which one `basquin-quarkus` build augments is untested.
- **A new design doc for follow-on work, DD-044 / PR-3.5**: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-preinstrumented-targets-design.md`, letting the operator drive a build-time-instrumented target without patching it, plus its own §8.1 experiment at `bench-results/dd044-native-jto-2026-07-26/`. Note two different "§8.1"s are in play — DD-043's Apicurio question and DD-044's native-flags question.
- Six PR-3 follow-ups recorded in `TODO.md` (two closed, four open), each with why it was deferred.

## What this does NOT establish

- The offline-JaCoCo **plugin execution** was not injected. §8.2 stands unmeasured — PR-4's entry gate.
- Both acceptances resolved over **localhost HTTP**; the real Pages HTTPS repo is unexercised until the first `v*` tag.
- **`rest-villains` native** remains unmeasured; the native cell ran on the fixture deliberately. PR-4's native 2×2 cells.
- ~~The verify script's `jvm` and `native` stages have never been executed.~~ **No longer true, and this line was stale for three rounds.** All five stages now run end-to-end: `bench-results/verify-20260730T215842Z/RESULTS.md:4` records `Stages run: unit jar guards jvm native`. (An earlier version of this line cited a run directory a later commit deleted — round 11's finding 4.) I told a previous approver this disclosure was "retired" — I retired it in a PR comment and not here, which is verbatim the defect round 5 raised as S5 ("a disclosure retired only in a PR comment"), recurring in the body of the same PR one round later.
- The negative heap delta (`-684`) is a known **PR-5 `UNMEASURED` producer**, not a clean measurement.

mode `Enabled`, box idle (0 compute apps via `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps` immediately
before each measurement pass), transparent hugepage `always [madvise] never` (recorded,
not forced), every measurement invocation pinned `taskset -c 4-7,20-23`. Boot
2026-07-10, no reboot across the session; driver `595.71.05` (matches the calibration
file). Box: `epyc7351-2080ti` (bare-metal EPYC 7351 / RTX 2080 Ti, per the memory index's
bench-machines distinction — this is not the WSL2 documentation box).

**Fresh calibration** (`bench/results/bp_calibration_epyc7351-2080ti.json`):
`pcie_under_load` gen `3`, width `16`; `triad_gbps` **25.9** — consistent with the
in-protocol pinned precedents (v1: 26.07, v2_gen3: 26.14). The "≈44" figure that floats
in older docs is the R1-era **pre-pinning** value and does not apply here.

**Row counts**: matrix sweep **289** `[verified]` / 0 VERIFY FAILED / 16 T2
(`transpose_quant`) `b_pipelined` N/A (chunkability audit, issue #114) / 79
duplicate-sweep-point skips (chunk ≥ full-buffer size collapsing to fewer effective
chunk counts, pre-existing tool behavior). R-sweep: **339** `[verified]` / 0 failures.

**Incident A**: the first matrix-run launch died when a subagent session ended
mid-run (~143 rows produced); the partial CSV was deleted and **both** sweeps were
re-run cleanly, in one supervised session, under the same ritual + calibration. The
committed CSVs (`bp_matrix_nsweep_epyc7351-2080ti.csv`, `bp_rsweep_epyc7351-2080ti.csv`)
are from that clean session only — no rows from the killed run are present.

**Incident B** (disclosed explicitly): the first targeted-rerun pass was measured at
`--threads 1` — the plan's own example command omitted `--threads 8` and the binary
silently defaults to 1 — and was committed as `34a498e`. This was caught during task
review via the data itself: CPU-staging methods (`a`, partially `b`) came back
systematically 1.3–6.2x slower than the frozen originals with stable (non-noisy) IQR,
which is the signature of a configuration defect, not hardware variance (`b_fair` /
`b_pipelined` do no CPU staging and were unaffected). Regenerated with `--threads 8` in
`f9f3030` per plan amendment `f5051c0`. Both passes exist in git history for
traceability; only the threads=8 files (`bp_matrix_nsweep_rerun_epyc7351-2080ti.csv`,
`bp_rsweep_rerun_epyc7351-2080ti.csv`) are current. Threads=8 rerun-vs-original ratios
over all 25 flagged points: mean **0.972**, range **0.866x–1.066x**.

**Unstable/rerun list**: 25 flagged best-chunk points (IQR/median > 5%) collapsing to 22
unique `(id, N)` invocations (10 matrix, 12 rsweep — one invocation per point re-measures
all methods together). Full verbatim flagged list and per-point original-vs-rerun
comparison table (from `.superpowers/sdd/2026-08-10-bp3-measurement/task-3-report.md`):


`gates.py --exp bp` merges originals+reruns by best-of-max per cell, which is **not**
the pre-declared stabler-preference (lower-IQR) merge rule
(`docs/r2-exp2-gen4-crossover.md:48-58`); CM5 must implement the stabler-preference
merge itself rather than reusing the gate's merge.

## Nsys digest

```
NSYS=/usr/local/cuda-12.5/bin/nsys
taskset -c 4-7,20-23 "$NSYS" profile -t cuda,osrt --force-overwrite true \
  -o "$SCRATCHDIR/bp_bpipelined_trace" \
  ./bench-rtrack --transform T1 --method bpipe --n 8192 --chunk-mib 16 \
  --warmup 2 --iters 8 --no-verify --csv /dev/null
```

nsys `2024.2.3.38-242334140272v0`. Over 160 launches: memcpy H2D total **205.6ms**
vs. kernel total **22.7ms** (~9x) — the GPU kernel is almost entirely hidden under
the H2D transfer in the two-stream pipelined design, consistent with
`h2d_occupancy ≈ 0.99` for this row class. Full digest committed at
`bench/results/bp_bpipelined_trace_2080ti.stats.txt`.

## Session status

Both boxes have landed: Gen3 (bare-metal EPYC 7351 / 2080 Ti) and Gen4 (WSL2 7800X3D /
4070 Ti SUPER) each ran the full protocol — fresh under-load calibration, matrix + r-sweep
`--method all`, targeted `--threads 8` reruns of flagged unstable best-chunk points — per
issue #116. The Gen4 runbook this PR added to `bench/rtrack/README.md` now carries its
as-executed notes. PR undrafted.

## Commit-order note

This PR creates the **first** `bp_*` artifacts in the repo. CM4 (`cm4_registered_predictions.json`,
`cm4_bimodal_cells.json`, merged `7097e94`) and BP2 (`gates.py --exp bp`, merged
`ddd573d`, PR #123) were both merged **prior** to any `bp_*` data existing, on the
explicit understanding that the gate/registration code would be validated against real
data once it landed. That acceptance is hereby finalized: the gates ran cleanly (see
above) against real full-protocol Gen3 data with no code changes needed.

Refs #116, #108, #115, #112

items.title: Topic 19: CPU frontend bottlenecks
items.body:
## Summary

- Adds Topic 19's compact mental model and a checked Rust cycle-accounting model.
- Adds a generated-C final-layout experiment with 512 equal leaf functions.
- Compares 16-byte and 4096-byte function spacing with 12 ABBA/BAAB blocks, 48 fresh processes, and a hard-linked A/A control.
- Retains exact-source host records, final ELF inspection, PMU attempt data, and full validation logs for `xxl` and `alg`.

## Exact-source evidence

Both hosts ran commit `cf1b205058a6985eac98dc70ef1b2ff1e35370c2` from archive SHA-256 `717e59c0dc7284bbeb8749da6229d96004417acdcef79e9619cb36cfc9d52a21`.

- `xxl`, Intel Xeon Platinum 8488C: sparse/dense ratio 7.383368103, 95% block interval [6.688401183, 8.150546454], 12 blocks and 48 timing processes. Retired instructions stayed nearly equal while DSB-delivered operations fell and MITE-delivered operations rose.
- `alg`, Arm implementer 0x41 part 0xd40: sparse/dense ratio 3.373277553, 95% block interval [3.359216483, 3.387397481], 12 blocks and 48 timing processes. L1I refill and instruction-TLB walk events rose in the sparse arm.
- Both A/A intervals contain one.
- The treatment changes the complete frontend footprint. The records do not assign a causal share to one cache, translation, prediction, or delivery structure.

## Sources

- Intel VTune CPU Metrics Reference: https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/docs/vtune-profiler/user-guide/2026-1/cpu-metrics-reference.html
- Intel software-development manuals: https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html
- Yasin, Top-Down Method: https://doi.org/10.1109/ISPASS.2014.6844459
- Arm Neoverse V1 frontend description: https://developer.arm.com/community/arm-community-blogs/b/architectures-and-processors-blog/posts/neoverse-v1-platform-a-new-performance-tier-for-arm
- Arm Neoverse V2 TRM: https://documentation-service.arm.com/static/633fe1ec4c59b30b517730b8
- Linux perf-stat documentation: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man1/perf-stat.1.html

## Validation

Passed locally and inside both exact-source Linux archives:

- `git diff --check`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test --workspace --lib --examples`
- `cargo test --workspace --doc`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo bench --workspace --no-run`
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`
- Python bytecode compilation and `bash -n` for the experiment scripts
- Correctness smoke checks, final-symbol/layout checks, focused disassembly, paired timing, A/A, PMU integrity, and before/after source-manifest equality

Documentation verification passed 75/75 claims with zero findings. A separate raw-evidence audit passed after checking host facts, source identities, statistics, code generation, counters, counter failures, and archive hashes.

This adds Topic 19 material on CPU frontend bottlenecks. It provides a checked Rust cycle-accounting model and a reproducible dense-versus-sparse layout experiment across Intel and Arm hosts, with retained evidence and explicit limits on causal claims.

## Why it was needed

The repository lacked a focused model and measurement method for CPU frontend supply limits. This change adds both without attributing observed slowdowns to one specific cache, predictor, translation structure, or delivery mechanism.

## How it works

- `src/lib.rs` models frontend supply, path switches, refills, translation penalties, redirects, phase cycle floors, and cold-code outlining. It rejects invalid, non-finite, and overflowing inputs.
- `examples/cost_model.rs` runs the model and reports cycle estimates, outlining costs, and the benefit decision.
- `experiment/generate.py` creates a C benchmark with 512 equal, aligned, `noinline` leaf functions, indirect calls, warmup and measurement phases, monotonic timing, and checksum validation.
- `experiment/frontend_experiment.py` validates output and ELF layout, runs alternating ABBA/BAAB timing blocks, analyzes geometric ratios, selects architecture-specific `perf` passes, and writes structured evidence.
- `experiment/run_remote.sh` validates source provenance, tool resolution, Cargo and Git configuration, CPU pinning, and output isolation. It rejects imported shell functions, aliases, `BASH_ENV`, hidden workspace members, repository-boundary escapes, and environment overrides. It cleans rejected scratch directories, stabilizes ELF hashes with a debug-prefix map, runs quality gates, builds both layouts, verifies hard-linked A/A controls, and archives host and binary evidence.
- Measurement reports retain source archives, hashes, layout inspection, timing results, PMU attempts, validation logs, and interpretation limits.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Changed: methodology and references] -->|model assumptions and evidence rules| B[Changed: Rust frontend model]
    B -->|cycle estimates| C[Changed: cost model example]
    D[New: C benchmark generator] -->|generated source| E[Changed: experiment driver]
    E -->|timing, layout, and PMU records| F[New: measurement reports and raw archives]
    G[New: remote runner] -->|validated builds and host evidence| E

    classDef changed fill:`#fff4cc`,stroke:`#d4a017`,stroke-width:2px
    classDef new fill:`#d4f4dd`,stroke:`#2e7d32`,stroke-width:2px

    class D,F,G new
```

The experiment compared 16-byte and 4096-byte function spacing across 12 timing blocks and 48 fresh processes. The sparse/dense ratio was `7.383368103` on Intel Xeon Platinum 8488C and `3.373277553` on Arm implementer `0x41`, part `0xd40`. Both A/A controls had a ratio of one.

## Key decisions

- The experiment changes function spacing while keeping generated program logic identical.
- Fresh processes and alternating block order reduce process-state and order effects.
- Hard-linked A/A binaries provide an identical-artifact control.
- PMU data is retained when available. Failed or unavailable counters do not invalidate timing results.
- The runner isolates build state and toolchain inputs. It validates source manifests and rejects environment and repository-boundary escapes.
- Archive documentation distinguishes recomputable reporting defects from limitations in measurement provenance and causal attribution. It does not present corrected metadata as regenerated measurements.
- The reports limit the conclusion to a change across the frontend footprint. They do not claim a universal alignment threshold or isolate one microarchitectural structure.

## Review focus

- Check input validation and overflow handling in the Rust model.
- Check timing-ratio and confidence-interval calculations.
- Check architecture-specific PMU selection and handling of unavailable or zero results.
- Check that retained archive corrections do not imply regenerated measurements.

items.title: Tell the truth about the PII model (OpenMed claim) and wire a real medical NER if one exists
items.body:
## Robinson issue answered

**Issue #2.** `architecture-notes.md:41`, the tech-stack table, and `README.md` claimed step 2 used "OpenMed (French medical NER, 97.97% F1, 55+ entity types)". The code (`src/phenoscribe/pii.py`) loaded `Jean-Baptiste/camembert-ner`: a general 4-label French NER (PER/LOC/ORG/MISC). It is not OpenMed, not medical, and the 97.97%-to-four-sig-figs claim had no citation.

What the research found:
- **OpenMed** is real (380+ NER models, Apache 2.0), but its NER heads target *English biomedical* disease/drug/pharma entities. There is no French PII NER named "OpenMed" that this code ever loaded.
- `Jean-Baptiste/camembert-ner` reports overall F1 **0.8914** on WikiNER (not 0.9797), with 4 general labels.
- [`Anonym-IA/V2-camembert-ner-pii-french`](https://huggingface.co/Anonym-IA/V2-camembert-ner-pii-french) is a genuine French *PII* NER: CamemBERT-base (110M, ~445 MB), MIT, validation micro-F1 **0.9327** (`best_metrics.json`), 39 BIO entity types (names, address, city/postal, email, phone, social-security number, IBAN, dates, job titles, ...). It loads and runs locally in seconds.

## What changed

- **New default PII model**: `Anonym-IA/V2-camembert-ner-pii-french`, wired as the configurable default. `pii.model`, `pii.fallback_model`, `pii.min_score` added to `config.yaml` and `Config` (new `PIIConfig`).
- **Offline fallback kept**: `Jean-Baptiste/camembert-ner` loads automatically if the default cannot be fetched, so the pipeline still works offline with whatever is cached.
- **Label mapping**: `pii.py` maps both models' labels into the existing pseudonym categories (`LABEL_TO_CATEGORY`). The regex layer (dates, Belgian/French phones, emails, Belgian national numbers) is unchanged and model-independent.
- **Docs corrected** (`README.md`, `context/architecture-notes.md`): state exactly which model runs and what it detects; removed the OpenMed / 97.97% / 55-entity-types claims; added a "what it catches, what it misses" section documenting that general/PII NER under-redacts rare hospital/clinic/drug-eponym names.

## Measurement / test results

Full suite: **49 passed** (was 41 before; +8 new PII tests, no regressions).

New tests (`tests/test_pii.py`):
- Regex redacts email/phone/date/Belgian national number (offline, stubbed NER).
- PII-model labels (NOM_PERSONNE, VILLE, NOM_SOCIETE) map to PERSON/LOCATION/ORGANIZATION.
- Fallback labels (PER/LOC/ORG) still map correctly.
- Same value gets one stable pseudonym; low-confidence detections dropped.
- **No-drift guards**: `PIIConfig()` and `config.yaml` both equal `pii.DEFAULT_MODEL`/`FALLBACK_MODEL`; the configured model actually loads (skips if hub offline).

Real comparison on the 4 cached (already-pseudonymised) transcripts:

| Transcript | Default PII NER finds | General fallback finds |
|---|---|---|
| 038 | 5 PERSON (e.g. "Madame de Simon", "Esposito") | 6 PERSON + 6 MISC (incl. drugs: Zaldiar, Ivabradine, Belozal) |
| 451 | 0 | 1 PERSON + 4 MISC (POTS, Covid, Internet, "Covid long") |
| 454 | 0 | 3 MISC (GSM, Covid, Paxlovid) |
| 467 | 0 | 0 |

The PII model focuses on identity and leaves drug/condition names intact (clinically useful). The general fallback over-redacts those as MISC, and it catches some first names the PII model misses (e.g. "Eloïse"). Honest tradeoff: neither is a complete de-identifier; the regex layer is exact for its patterns; spot-check the first batch.

## Robinson Test

Moves **Q "are the stated tools the tools actually used?"** (docs now match code, enforced by a drift test) and **Q "is the privacy/PII claim honest and defensible?"** (real model, cited F1, documented recall limits).

items.title: docs/06 + enlightenment experiment: grokking as 悟り, and R1 finally measured
items.body:
## What this is

You shared your essay on 悟り — enlightenment as taking off the 色眼鏡 (colored glasses = 思い込み) one by one until you reach the true world a newborn already sees — and connected it to grokking. This folds that essay into the repo's measured arc, held to `00-charter-and-discipline.md`, the same way `docs/05` folded in your insight/crystallization model.

## The mapping

| essay | measured mechanism |
|---|---|
| 色眼鏡, stacked thousands deep | excess weight norm above the structural minimum (memorizer ‖w‖≈270 vs structure ≈122) |
| taking them off one by one | norm reduction (H-rep Phase 3) |
| the true world (always there behind the glasses) | the low-norm structural Fourier circuit — grokking *uncovers* it |
| the newborn baby, born seeing | the transparent medium (C2): no glasses to remove, no memorization phase |
| the last glass = consciousness | metaphor only — a vanilla MLP has no self-model |

## Why it earns an experiment

The essay's core claim — the adult who removes his glasses and the baby who never wore them see **the same true world** — is exactly **R1** (charter 1.3: "a grokked and a smoothly-learned solution *may* be the identical circuit"), which the repo asserts but has **never measured**. `docs/06` pre-registers the test; `experiments/enlightenment/analyze.py` runs it, measuring per-unit spectra of the learned fc1 weights in residue space (Nanda-style).

## Result (single seed, p=97)

| net | role | val_acc | ‖w‖ | **per_unit_top1** |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| onehot wd=1.0 (grokked) | adult, glasses off | 1.000 | 122.8 | **0.879** |
| onehot wd=0.0 (memorizer) | glasses on | 0.024 | 270.5 | **0.322** |
| fourier nf=1 (transparent) | baby | 0.896 | 289.5 | 1.000† |

*(flat baseline 0.021; † trivial — the nf=1 input is one sinusoid)*

**Supported.** The opaque grokker makes each hidden unit a near-clean sinusoid (0.879) — it rebuilds the Fourier structure behind the glasses — while the memorizer stays structureless (0.322). **Generalizing ⟺ a Fourier representation.** R1 goes from assertion to result: the two paths share the same harmonic vocabulary.

**Corrected (pre-registered wrong, reported honestly).** The essay's "one" world / the memo's "few frequencies" is wrong about the *count*: each unit is one frequency, but the population spans **all 48 harmonics**. Fewness was a property of the transparent *input*, not the grokked *solution*. So the adult and the baby reach the same *kind* of world (harmonic), not the identical vector — the medium pins *which* frequencies, which sharpens C2.

**Mirage guard.** The population-averaged spectrum cannot separate grok from memorize (0.15 vs 0.14); the discrimination lives entirely in the per-unit metric.

**Honest dis-analogy (kept, `docs/06` §3).** Removing the *last* glass — driving ‖w‖→0 — is death (underfit), not enlightenment. The network's "true world" is the minimum sufficient structure, not the mystic's emptiness.

## Files

- `docs/06-enlightenment.md` — design memo, mapping, pre-registered prediction, outcome, dis-analogy
- `experiments/enlightenment/analyze.py` — the measurement (reuses the verified harness/model)
- `experiments/enlightenment/results/spectrum.json` — the record (full per-unit + population spectra)
- `experiments/enlightenment/RESULTS_enlightenment.md` — measured outcome + honest bounds
- `README.md` — Status bullet added

## Bounds

Single seed / single config; a seed sweep is owed. `per_unit_top1` proves *sinusoidal*, not a *working* trig circuit — confirming operand units share a frequency and the output reads the product is the Nanda-style follow-up, not done here.

The release sweep must review the entire v0.8.0..HEAD history, including objective 5 in #162 and the CI workflow fix #163; review scope is the whole release delta, not merely this release commit or branch diff. Validate exact coverage against the 92.5 floor and report the total. Confirm every byte-pinned generated document and README transcript matches its builder (docs/example-output.md, docs/report.html, docs/showcase.html, docs/audiences.html, docs/nesyarena-conformance-report.md, README transcripts), verify pack/engine/requirement counts in digits and words, and check cross-document coherence including diagrams, docs/semantics.md test references, and docs/README.md index. Do not merge and do not create a GitHub Release; stop at the green PR/CI-ready point and report the PR URL, exact coverage, and what the review actually examined. The branch was rebased onto current origin/main before the version bump; #163 halves checks to six per push, which is expected. ## What Changed - **0.9.0 cut.** `[Unreleased]` is promoted to `[0.9.0] - 2026-08-11` and its release account rewritten against the whole v0.8.0..HEAD delta (including #162's measured semantics gap and #163's workflow fix), with the version agreeing in `pyproject.toml`, the topmost released `CHANGELOG.md` heading, `src/reasonsmith/__init__.py` and `CITATION.cff`; a fresh empty `[Unreleased]` is left behind. - **Behaviour corrections found reviewing that delta.** `PairedReplayEngine` now returns *not evaluated* (`some_replays_failed`) whenever any planned pair raises on the satisfaction path instead of clearing the duty from the pairs that answered, and `_pair_membership` treats any failure to evaluate a constraint — not just `UnsupportedConstructError` — as undetermined; the certificate engine names the *worst* offending decision index rather than the first; `artifacts.reference_semantics` canonicalises an accepted spelling and carries an unrecognised one instead of raising mid-audit, with `Certificate.__post_init__` and `semantic_laws` normalising through the same vocabulary; the drift verification manifest moves to schema version 2 carrying a `quote_corpus_sha256` over (pack, requirement, quote), which `published_counts()` refuses against so a stale clearance cannot be published, and `reasonsmith published-counts` reports that refusal on stderr with exit 1 instead of tracebacking; `autoformalize.signoff` reports `missing` when no refinement record is on disk. - **Pointer and prose repairs after the README reorganisation** across the three workflows, `tests/conftest.py`, the CLI docstring and epilogue, `report.py`'s schema-version note, `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `ROADMAP.md` and `docs/` (adopting, autoformalization, semantics, three-systems, example-output), plus vulnerability reports routed to `SECURITY.md` before public channels — with new tests in ten test modules pinning each fix above. ## Risk Assessment ⚠️ Medium: The release cut itself verifies correct (version agreement in all four places, complete PR coverage of the v0.8.0..HEAD delta, byte pins untouched), but twelve fixer rounds layered real behaviour changes into it — a shipped counterfactual verdict moved from satisfied/probed to not-evaluated, published-counts gained hard refusals, artefact-semantics normalization changed at three boundaries — each documented and tested, with only one low-reach contract regression left. ## Testing Ran the targeted test set covering the release intent — release discipline, published counts, all byte-pinned generated documents and README transcripts, cross-document coherence, and every module touched by the v0.8.0..HEAD delta — roughly 200 tests across 22 modules, all passing. Beyond the tests I demonstrated the release the way a user meets it: the CLI reports 0.9.0 and all four version sites agree with the `[0.9.0] - 2026-08-11` heading above a fresh empty `[Unreleased]`; re-running all five document builders left the worktree completely clean, which is direct proof that docs/report.html, docs/audiences.html, docs/showcase.html, the README transcripts and docs/nesyarena-conformance-report.md still match their builders; the rendered dossier was captured in a real browser and shows the correct headline and verdicts; the shipped violating example runs end to end and reports its breach; and the docs/README.md index has no dangling or missing entries. The only intent item I could not deliver is the exact coverage total, which requires the full suite this phase is barred from running — the floor mechanism itself is validated and CI owns the number, so I raised that as a warning for the user to decide on. No PR exists on this branch yet, so no PR URL to report; that phase belongs to the outer executor. - Evidence: Rendered docs/report.html — the generated conformance dossier as published (local file: /tmp/no-mistakes-evidence/01KZRQNC6CFBPRNR9YEMHB39X3/report-html-top.png)
Evidence: Four-site version agreement at 0.9.0 $ reasonsmith --version reasonsmith 0.9.0 $ python -c "import reasonsmith; print(reasonsmith.__version__)" 0.9.0 $ grep -n ^version pyproject.toml CITATION.cff pyproject.toml:7:version = "0.9.0" CITATION.cff:10:version: "0.9.0" $ grep -m2 "^## \[" CHANGELOG.md ## [Unreleased] ## [0.9.0] - 2026-08-11 ```text $ reasonsmith --version reasonsmith 0.9.0 $ python -c "import reasonsmith; print(reasonsmith.__version__)" 0.9.0 $ grep -n ^version pyproject.toml CITATION.cff pyproject.toml:7:version = "0.9.0" CITATION.cff:10:version: "0.9.0" $ grep -m1 "^## \[" CHANGELOG.md ; grep -m2 "^## \[" CHANGELOG.md ## [Unreleased] ## [0.9.0] - 2026-08-11 ```
Evidence: Every generated document reproduces from its builder with zero drift $ python docs/build_example.py $ python docs/build_audiences.py $ python docs/build_showcase.py $ python docs/build_readme_transcripts.py $ python docs/build_nesyarena_report.py wrote docs/nesyarena-conformance-report.md $ git status --porcelain # every generated doc byte-identical to its builder (exit: no output above = no drift) ```text $ python docs/build_example.py $ python docs/build_audiences.py $ python docs/build_showcase.py $ python docs/build_readme_transcripts.py $ python docs/build_nesyarena_report.py wrote docs/nesyarena-conformance-report.md $ git status --porcelain # every generated doc byte-identical to its builder (exit: no output above = no drift) ```
Evidence: Shipped violating example run on the 0.9.0 tree $ python -m reasonsmith.examples.truncating_credit_system CONFORMANCE REPORT system: TruncatingCreditSystem (top-k truncation at k=1, inference artefact exposed) declared domains: consumer-credit pack: ecoa:ecoa_reg_b_1002_9_b_2_principal_reasons_complete headline: 1 requirements · 1 binding: 1 violated REQUIREMENT FINDINGS: [PROBED] ecoa_reg_b_1002_9_b_2_principal_reasons_complete: violated certificate finding: FAIL (decision 1) offending record: decision APP-1042 (step 1) ```text $ python -m reasonsmith.examples.truncating_credit_system CONFORMANCE REPORT system: TruncatingCreditSystem (top-k truncation at k=1, inference artefact exposed) declared scope: undeclared declared domains: consumer-credit pack: ecoa:ecoa_reg_b_1002_9_b_2_principal_reasons_complete headline: 1 requirements · 1 binding: 1 violated REQUIREMENT FINDINGS: [PROBED] ecoa_reg_b_1002_9_b_2_principal_reasons_complete (ECOA / Regulation B (12 CFR 1002.9) 12 CFR 1002.9(b)(2)): violated evidence basis: artifact — this duty is measured against the inference artefact behind a decision rather than against what the system decided. No trace holds that artefact and the enumeration is exact only on the one artefact it ran over, so the rungs above unattainable are recounted and probed, and neither observed nor proved is reachable however much the system exposes. Which of the two a verdict reaches is a fact about the artefact and not about the search: probed measures a reason set enumerated from a model encoding, recounted measures one the system recounted about its own inference. requires: artifact_logs_reason_explanation, artifact_logs_deleted_reason_count domain limit: consumer-credit summary: Violated on 1 of 2 certified decision(s): the stated reasons are not all the reasons. On decision #1 exact inference found 5 reason(s) and the deletion probe showed the system's answer does not depend on 4 of them — C05 — Insufficient number of credit references provided; C03 — Delinquent past or present credit obligations; C04 — Too many recent inquiries on credit bureau report; C02 — Length of time credit has been established is too short. Point the inventory/demo references to their actual destinations and describe the current pull-request/main-push trigger. 🔧 Fix: fix proposer packaging, certificate attribution, and release coherence 7 issues (5 errors, 2 warnings) still open: - 🚨 `src/reasonsmith/published_counts.py:49` - The verification manifest is validated only by aggregate counts. After a successful drift run, changing or replacing any statutory quote without changing the total leaves `match == quote_count` and `differ == 0`, so `published_counts()` falsely reports the modified corpus as verified. Bind the manifest to requirement IDs and quote bytes (for example with a deterministic corpus digest) and verify that binding before emitting `verified`. - 🚨 `src/reasonsmith/engines/counterfactual.py:1082` - The new cross-rung diagnostic evaluates declared constraints against logged values but catches only `UnsupportedConstructError`. A valid numeric constraint such as `income + 1 > 0` with a logged string value raises `TypeError`; after proof satisfaction and replay violation, `_residual()` reaches this path and crashes the entire conformance report instead of preserving the proof with `membership_undetermined`. Treat constraint-evaluation failures as undetermined at this diagnostic boundary. - 🚨 `src/reasonsmith/engines/counterfactual.py:1192` - The new diagnostic treats every `proved=violated`/`probed=satisfied` pair as proof that the log does not exercise the declared space. However, paired replay returns `SATISFIED` whenever at least one pair completes, even if other planned pairs raised (lines 1017-1042). A system can therefore raise on the discriminating pair, complete another unchanged pair, and receive this incorrect cause. Enforce complete evidence at the shared paired-replay boundary by returning not evaluated when any planned pair errors; then the cross-rung signal will not consume a partial satisfaction. - ⚠️ `src/reasonsmith/certificate.py:197` - `normalize_claimed_semantics()` accepts canonicalizable case/whitespace, but `Certificate.__post_init__` discards its return value. Thus an out-of-tree artefact claiming `" Distribution Semantics "` passes validation but remains raw and is rejected as mismatching canonical `exact_semantics`; `semantic_laws.law_refusal` similarly reads the raw attribute directly. `reference_semantics` also accepts any string despite its protocol requiring a vocabulary member. Canonicalize both semantics fields at their public boundaries so accepted spellings cannot produce false refusals. - 🚨 `ROADMAP.md:8` - The required release sweep says to review objective 5 and maintain cross-document coherence. Objective 5 is now marked closed and its measurable outcome passes, but this overview—and AGENTS.md:807-809—still says every objective has an outcome that “fails today.” Update both descriptions to distinguish open outcomes from closed, passing ones. - 🚨 `CHANGELOG.md:32` - The required v0.9.0 release account must be accurate, but this entry promises a solver witness for every non-equivalent result. `round_trip_check()` returns stronger/weaker/incomparable temporal results without witnesses (autoformalize.py:594-600), and differing counterfactual atoms return incomparable with only a reason (lines 544-550). Either limit the claim to the logical/state fragment or implement witnesses for those fragments; docs/autoformalization.md:35-37 repeats the overclaim. - ⚠️ `CHANGELOG.md:40` - CONTRIBUTING.md requires every changelog entry to link its introducing PR, but several v0.9.0 entries remain unlinked: lines 40 (#155), 49 and 52 (#158), 55 (#147), 58 (#144), 61 (#143), 64 (#145), and 72 (#146). Add the corresponding links to complete the release discipline mechanically. 🔧 Fix: harden release provenance, replay, semantics, and documentation 4 issues (1 warning, 3 infos) still open: - ⚠️ `CHANGELOG.md:11` - Intent requires the [0.9.0] account be "accurate against the complete v0.8.0..HEAD delta", and the account's own #163 entry sets the standard ("the account of this release is the whole `v0.8.0..HEAD` delta, not the product-facing part of it"). Commit a375fec changed a shipped verdict and the account records nothing. At v0.8.0, `git show 7d666ea:src/reasonsmith/engines/counterfactual.py:984` returned SATISFIED at `probed` with the note "N pair(s) raised and were counted rather than read as a pass"; HEAD returns not evaluated (`some_replays_failed`, counterfactual.py:1025-1033). A system whose `decide()` raises on some protected twins was `satisfied`/`probed` on `gdpr_art22_1_no_prohibited_decision_for_any_input`-shaped counterfactual duties in 0.8.0 and is `inconclusive`/not evaluated in 0.9.0. `PairedReplayEngine` predates 0.8.0 (#102), so this is a cross-release change, not an intra-release detail. It also sits under the #147 entry whose text says "Nothing here moves a verdict, a strength or a witness". Add an entry (the rule is the right one — it is what `probed.py:757-773` and docs/formal.md:907-910 already enforce for the sibling search — but it must be recorded). - ℹ️ `docs/semantics.md:1196` - The `satisfied at probed` guarantee box for paired replay ends "the budget on the result names the pairs replayed, the values used and the pairs that raised", which reads as though a satisfied paired-replay verdict can sit beside pairs that raised. After counterfactual.py:1025-1033 it cannot: `pairs_errored` is now necessarily 0 in any satisfied result. The sibling statement for the ordinary replay search is spelled out at docs/formal.md:907-910 ("A search in which *any* planned input raised is *not evaluated* rather than satisfied over the part that answered"); this box should state the same rule for pairs, naming `test_partial_replay_evidence_never_becomes_satisfaction_or_a_cross_rung_cause`. - ℹ️ `tests/test_drift.py:297` - The invariant the round-8 fix introduced is that the manifest `drift.main --verification-manifest` writes is the one `published_counts()` accepts. Neither side tests that. tests/test_drift.py:297 compares the written digest against `quote_corpus_sha256` called on the same `report.results`, and tests/test_published_counts.py:71-77 hand-builds a manifest from the same helper — both assert the helper equals itself, so a divergence between drift's `(pack_id, requirement_id, quote)` triple and published_counts' `(pack.id, requirement.id, requirement.verbatim_text)` triple would pass. One test that runs the drift writer over the shipped statutory packs and then asserts `published_counts()` reports `status == "verified"` against that file would pin the actual binding. - ℹ️ `AGENTS.md:602` - Residual of the already-approved cross-document coherence sweep. AGENTS.md:602 states "The README's first screen after the badges is that run and its transcript, then docs/what-this-does-not-do.md — the theory sections, the four things this tool cannot do, and both preview images live below the fold and nothing may move them back above it." In the current README the transcript is at README.md:55 under *Install and run*, below the mermaid diagram and the five reading paths; the two preview images (docs/assets/showcase-figure.svg, showcase-cast.svg) are at README.md:9 and :11, i.e. above everything rather than below the fold; and *Limits* carries six bullets, not four. The neighbouring paragraph at AGENTS.md:555 describes the same first screen differently. CLAUDE.md is a symlink to AGENTS.md, so one edit covers both. 🔧 Fix: document paired-replay completeness and verify manifest handoff 4 issues (2 warnings, 2 infos) still open: - ⚠️ `CHANGELOG.md:30` - Intent requires the [0.9.0] account be "accurate against the complete v0.8.0..HEAD delta". The new paired-replay entry closes with ([#147](.../pull/147)), but #147 contains none of this change. `git log -S "counted rather than read as a pass" -- src/reasonsmith/engines/counterfactual.py` returns exactly two commits: 79e0790 ("counterfactual invariance under one named protected variable (#102)"), which introduced the count-and-pass behaviour before v0.8.0, and a375fec, this branch's own fix commit, which replaced it. So the entry credits a PR that neither introduced nor changed the behaviour. The same file already handles this correctly twice: the #161 entry says "The refusal itself is 0.8.0's ... this release does not change that behaviour", and #147's own entry at line 63 now says "the paired-replay completeness change recorded above is separate". Attribute this entry to the release PR (or state that it was made in the release sweep), not to #147. - ⚠️ `docs/semantics.md:920` - The sentence reads "the source-derived declaration inventory is checked by `test_every_shipped_artefact_family_exposes_only_normalized_claims`". That test (tests/test_claimed_semantics.py:78) is not source-derived: it hand-constructs one `GroundProgramArtifact` and one `ReasonTraceArtifact` and asserts their claims. The test it replaced walked `src/reasonsmith/**/*.py` with `ast` and asserted every `claimed_semantics` literal in the tree was a vocabulary member. Removing the AST scan was correct per the test-quality rule, but the doc sentence was only renamed, not re-derived, so it now promises drift protection the suite does not provide: a third artefact family (or any other `claimed_semantics = "..."` assignment) added later with an out-of-vocabulary literal is caught by no test, and `tests/test_docs_semantics.py` only checks that the named test exists, not that the description matches it. The related [0.9.0] entry at CHANGELOG.md:15 carries the same claim ("including that every declaration shipped in this tree is a member"). Either reword both to describe the per-family check, or enumerate the families from a registry so the test is genuinely exhaustive. - ℹ️ `src/reasonsmith/semantic_laws.py:156` - `claimed = normalize_claimed_semantics(getattr(artifact, "claimed_semantics", ""))` — the `""` default was written so an artefact declaring nothing falls through to the module's own `NO_LAWS_FOR_SEMANTICS` refusal, which `law_refusal`'s signature (`-> str | None`) and docstring ("Why these laws cannot be checked against this artefact") promise. Wrapping it in the refusing normalizer makes that default a guaranteed `ValueError: '' is not a known claimed semantics value`: an artefact that satisfies `admits_interpretation` but exposes no `claimed_semantics` now crashes a public, exported function instead of being told why the laws do not apply. Canonicalization was the requested fix and is right for an accepted spelling; the tolerant path just needs to survive it — normalize inside a try and fall through to `NO_LAWS_FOR_SEMANTICS` on failure, or drop the now-dead default so the read is honest about requiring the attribute. - ℹ️ `src/reasonsmith/published_counts.py:62` - The `schema_version != 2` test is folded into the same branch as the digest test and raises "legal verification manifest does not match the statutory quote corpus". A manifest written by v0.8.0's `python -m reasonsmith.drift --verification-manifest` carries `schema_version: 1` and no `quote_corpus_sha256` at all (drift.py:511 bumped it to 2 in this delta), so an operator who kept a manifest from the previous release is told the statutory quotes have drifted — the one thing that manifest exists to deny — when the real cause is that it predates the digest. Split the schema check into its own `ValueError` naming the version it found and the regeneration command. 🔧 Fix: correct release attribution, semantics claims, and manifest refusals 4 issues (2 warnings, 2 infos) still open: - ⚠️ `src/reasonsmith/artifacts/__init__.py:179` - The round-8 fix replaced `return value if isinstance(value, str) else None` with `normalize_claimed_semantics(value) if value is not None else None`. Canonicalizing an accepted spelling was the approved change; refusing an unaccepted one was not, and it lands at the wrong site. `reference_semantics` is read inside a conformance run (`certificate.certify_artifact:645`), so an out-of-tree artefact family exposing `exact_semantics = "approximate WMC"` (or any non-string) now raises `ValueError`/`TypeError` out of `check_conformance` and crashes the whole report, where before it took the documented graceful path: `semantics_reference_refusal` returned the mismatch wording and the duty came back *not evaluated* naming the claim (`_mismatched_claim`, engines/certificate.py:580-594). The docstring immediately above still promises the tolerant contract — "Read with `getattr` and defaulting to **None** ... a family that does not say claims nothing" — and no longer describes the refusal. Either normalize tolerantly here (fall back to the raw value so the existing mismatch path fires) and keep the refusal at the artefact/certificate boundaries, or update the docstring and `test_reference_semantics_canonicalizes_and_refuses_unknown_values` to state that an unrecognised reference aborts the run rather than being reported. - ⚠️ `CHANGELOG.md:16` - Intent requires the [0.9.0] account be "accurate against the complete v0.8.0..HEAD delta". The Breaking entry says the closed vocabulary is "refused where it is written" and that an out-of-tree family "now stops constructing". Neither holds for the case it describes. `GroundProgramArtifact.claimed_semantics` is a property (artifacts/ground_program.py:88-90) — an adapter with a bogus label constructs fine and raises only on attribute read; the fix round's own `test_every_shipped_artefact_family_exposes_only_normalized_claims` pins exactly that (`with pytest.raises(...): _ = invalid_ground_program.claimed_semantics`). An out-of-tree family implementing the protocol directly is normalized nowhere at all — it constructs, and is refused at `Certificate.__post_init__` (certificate.py:196-201) partway through an audit. Only `ReasonTraceArtifact` (reason_trace.py:98) refuses at construction. That difference is the whole migration story for the adopter this entry addresses: they learn at audit time, not at import time. Reword to say where each family is actually refused. - ℹ️ `src/reasonsmith/engines/counterfactual.py:1087` - The round-8 fix widened `except UnsupportedConstructError` to a bare `except Exception:` and deleted the three-line comment that explained why an unreadable constraint is the third answer. Widening was the right call for the reported `TypeError` path, but as written any error class — a `RecursionError`, a bug in `parse_expression`, a `KeyError` from a malformed record — is silently reclassified as "the constraint's truth on this pair is unknown", with nothing recorded about what actually failed. Every sibling broad catch in this module carries `# noqa: BLE001 — <reason>` (lines 960, 972). Restore the rationale comment and consider naming the exception in the returned `undetermined` text so a diagnostic that eliminated nothing can be told from one that hit a defect. - ℹ️ `src/reasonsmith/published_counts.py:54` - Four consecutive `if verification is not None and ...` guards (lines 54, 58, 65, 67) accreted one per fix round. Collapse them into a single `if verification is not None:` block holding the four checks; the control flow is identical and the next check added won't repeat the guard a fifth time. 🔧 Fix: carry unknown semantics reference instead of raising mid-audit 1 info still open: - ℹ️ `src/reasonsmith/semantic_laws.py:156` - `law_refusal` promises `-> str | None` ("Why these laws cannot be checked against this artefact") and owns a `NO_LAWS_FOR_SEMANTICS` branch for exactly that case, but `claimed = "" if raw is None else normalize_claimed_semantics(raw)` raises `ValueError` for any string outside `spec.CLAIMED_SEMANTICS`. Round 11 repaired only the missing-attribute half; the out-of-vocabulary half still raises. At v0.8.0 the read was `getattr(artifact, "claimed_semantics", "")` and an artefact claiming `"max-join over proof scores"` got the refusal naming its claim, so this is a regression introduced by round 8. The two shipped families normalize on their own (property read / `__init__`), but a family implementing the `artifacts.InferenceArtifact` protocol directly is normalized nowhere — the exact case the [0.9.0] Breaking entry (CHANGELOG.md:16) documents — so `law_refusal(that_artefact)` raises out of a public exported function instead of refusing. `test_a_claim_outside_the_vocabulary_never_reaches_this_module` does not pin this: its artefact is a `GroundProgramArtifact`, so the raise comes from the property, and the test still passes if this call is made tolerant. Round 12 gave `artifacts.reference_semantics` the tolerant treatment (try/except ValueError, carry as written) for the same reason; mirror it here and fall through to `NO_LAWS_FOR_SEMANTICS`. Blast radius is out-of-tree callers only: nothing inside the package calls `law_refusal`/`check_laws`, and no requirement reads the measurement.
⚠️ **Test** - 1 warning - ⚠️ `.github/workflows/ci.yml:76` - Exact coverage total against the 92.5 floor could not be produced locally: it requires running the complete repository test suite, which this targeted-validation phase is explicitly barred from doing. The floor's *mechanism* is validated (`tests/test_release_discipline.py::test_the_coverage_floor_fails_a_total_below_it` passes, and `[tool.coverage.report] precision = 2` in pyproject.toml is present, so `--cov-fail-under=92.5` genuinely bites rather than rounding away). The number itself must come from the CI `pytest --cov=reasonsmith --cov-fail-under=92.5` step. The user should decide whether the CI-reported total satisfies the intent's "report the total" requirement. - `python -m pytest tests/test_release_discipline.py tests/test_published_counts.py` — version agreement across the four sites, fresh [Unreleased], pack/engine/requirement counts in digits and words, coverage-floor mechanism - `python -m pytest tests/test_docs_example_output.py tests/test_docs_showcase.py tests/test_docs_audiences.py tests/test_docs_readme_transcripts.py tests/test_html_report.py tests/test_docs_three_systems.py tests/test_docs_language_model.py` — byte-for-byte generated-document and README-transcript pins - `python -m pytest tests/test_docs_semantics.py tests/test_docs_refinement.py tests/test_docs_formal.py tests/test_docs_adopting.py tests/test_findings_nesyarena.py tests/test_nesyarena_conformance.py tests/test_language_definition.py` — cross-document coherence, semantics.md test references, refinement census, citation registry - `python -m pytest tests/test_claimed_semantics.py tests/test_semantic_laws.py tests/test_deviation_duty.py tests/test_counterfactual_invariance.py tests/test_sufficient_reasons.py tests/test_drift.py tests/test_autoformalize.py tests/test_proposer.py tests/test_ecoa_specific_reasons.py tests/test_artifact_protocol.py tests/test_certificate_engine.py tests/test_adoption_surface.py tests/test_packaged_examples.py` — every module touched by the v0.8.0..HEAD delta - Manual: `python -m reasonsmith.cli --version`, `python -c "import reasonsmith; print(reasonsmith.__version__)"`, `grep '^version' pyproject.toml CITATION.cff`, `grep -m2 '^## \[' CHANGELOG.md` — four-site version agreement transcript - Manual: re-ran `python docs/build_example.py`, `build_audiences.py`, `build_showcase.py`, `build_readme_transcripts.py`, `build_nesyarena_report.py` then `git status --porcelain` — empty output proves every committed generated file is byte-identical to its builder - Manual: `python -m reasonsmith.examples.truncating_credit_system` — shipped violating example runs end to end on the 0.9.0 tree and reports the breach with probe budget and certificate finding - Manual: `chrome-devtools-axi open file://$PWD/docs/report.html` + screenshot — rendered dossier surface as an end user sees it - Manual: parsed `docs/README.md` links against `docs/*.md` on disk — no dangling links, no unlinked documents
🔧 **Document** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - ℹ️ `CONTRIBUTING.md:100` - SECURITY.md was added in this release delta (#159) and CONTRIBUTING.md gained the matching Response times and Attribution convention sections, but CONTRIBUTING's *Reporting Issues* section still routes every reporter to Discussions or the issue templates and never mentions the private vulnerability address. GitHub surfaces SECURITY.md on its own, so nothing is wrong, and adding a pointer is an addition rather than a stale-fact fix — left out of this pass. Follow-up: one pointer line in *Reporting Issues* naming SECURITY.md as the owner for vulnerability reports. 🔧 Fix: route vulnerability reports to SECURITY.md before public channels ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

items.title: core: a mock answer may never be resumed into a real grid
items.body:
## What this cycle did

Found and closed a hole on this repo's own documented happy path, during a vendor cycle in the packs repo. Two further problems were filed rather than fixed.

## The defect

`run --mock` writes its per-condition runs into the **same** date-stamped results directory a real grid uses — only the mock *preflight* gets a directory of its own (`<date>-mock-preflight`, gitignored). The runner is resumable. So the dry-run sequence the README documents:

```bash
python -m core --packs-dir . factory next --queue queue.yaml --provider mock   # dry run, $0
python -m core --packs-dir . factory next --queue queue.yaml --model <id>      # the real cycle
```

produced, on the same day, a real grid that **resumed straight off the mock answers**, counted them as measured, and wrote a metadata block naming the real model and a real spend.

Observed directly: after a mock dispatch, `results/<date>-no-context/` and `results/<date>-public-docs/` existed carrying `metadata.mock: true`, `model: mock-model`, `n: 1`, with per-run archives whose `tool_discipline` key was absent — which the resume path reads as *passing*. The next real run would have reused all of them.

Publishing a mock number as a vendor's result is the worst failure this harness has available to it, and it required no mistake to reach — only following the documented sequence twice in one day.

## The fix

A provenance stamp, not a re-burn.

- A mock run writes `mock: true` on each archived record. **Only** on mock runs, so every real archive stays byte-identical — the same discipline `format_repaired` already follows.
- The reuse decision moved out of the loop into `may_reuse_archived_run(prev, *, is_mock)`, which refuses to let a mock archive stand in for a real run **or** a real archive for a mock dry-run. The converse matters: a dry-run that silently reused real answers would report a plumbing proof it never performed.
- **Absence of the stamp means "real"**, which is what it means for every archive written before the stamp existed. No committed result is invalidated, no re-burn is forced, and `rebuild-report`'s ability to re-score archives offline at zero model spend is untouched — that ability is how three previous cycles corrected published numbers.

The decision was extracted into a named function so it is testable without a live model, which is the only reason this has real coverage rather than a comment.

## Verification

- **Every rule verified by breaking it.** With the provenance check disabled, exactly three of the nine tests fail and the other six still pass; restoring makes all nine pass.
- Suite **534 → 552**. `pytest -m regression` **17 passed**; the frozen **73/68/93** is unmoved.
- Hazard registry **57 → 59**, all `gated_by` refs resolve, `adrs_with_no_recorded_hazard: []`.
- No scorer, parser, prompt or fixture touched.

## Registry entries

- `a-mock-answer-can-be-resumed-into-a-real-grid` — **gated**, naming the five tests.
- `run-provenance-is-recorded-only-as-an-absence` — **ungated**, and the honest residue: this reads a stamp and treats absence as "real", so it catches a mock archive and **not** a run archived under a different model, prompt contract or scorer version. A full provenance hash would catch the general case and would also invalidate every archive the moment any of the three changed — precisely what `rebuild-report` exists to avoid. Recorded rather than claimed as closed.

## Filed, not fixed

- **#27** — a mock grid should write to its own directory, so the collision is impossible rather than detected. Not done in-cycle because it changes where results land, which should not travel inside a vendor measurement.
- **#26** — fetch policy can only override `User-Agent`. A documentation host met this cycle gates on `Referer`: a plain fetch of its reference content returns **HTTP 200 with a ~11 KB substitute page** titled "Page Not Found", and the same URL with the header returns ~1 MB of real reference. This slips past ADR-0009 because the body is neither empty nor short — it would be hashed and archived as a healthy snapshot. Adoption has to be a cohort-wide re-baseline, never one vendor inside its own measurement, so it is filed rather than built.

## No ADR

Deliberate. This is a correctness fix to an existing contract, not a new decision — the resume rule already said "reuse a run that was a valid measurement"; it just failed to check one of the two things that makes one valid. The hazard registry carries the record.

## Not done

No history rewrite, no force push, no branch deletion, no PR merged, no issue closed or assigned — including the two filed here.

items.title: Sprint P0.3: fitness-data-sync truth review, Bing fixes, duplicate-data article, SEO/GEO master plan
items.body:
## Summary

Sprint P0.3 — production release of P0.2 (fitness-data-sync category) + Bing SEO fixes + the new duplicate-data article, plus a final truth audit and a permanent SEO/GEO strategy plan.

- **Truth audit (new this sprint)**: removed unsourced "90%/60%" stats and an unverifiable "hundreds of reports" framing from `health-connect-not-syncing` (11 locales); corrected a false claim in `esportare-dati-garmin` that described FitMesh as integrated with Garmin Connect "via the official API" — the real mechanism today is the Health Connect pass-through, the official Garmin Health API OAuth integration is Q3 2026 roadmap (verified against `lib/providers/data.ts`).
- **`/llms.txt`**: added a link to `/fitness-data-sync` and an export/write-back status line (Strava read live; Strava write/TrainingPeaks/RideWithGPS/Google Drive in development; Health Connect + Apple Health write-back live/opt-in) — previously missing entirely.
- **Bing fixes** (from a prior commit, re-verified this sprint): 2 titles ≤70c, 7 meta descriptions in the 150-160c range, NL `health-connect-not-syncing` noindex bug fixed.
- **New article** `piu-smartwatch-insieme-dati-doppi` / `multiple-smartwatches-duplicate-data` (IT/EN only, written by Codex in a separate worktree, independently re-verified here): distinguishes aggregate-total dedup from raw-record/workout dedup, explains source priority and sync-loop prevention, 8 official Android/Google source citations.
- **`docs/seo/seo-geo-master-plan.md`** (new): canonical strategy doc — mission, permanent principles, 2026-07-13 GSC/Bing baseline, P0-P3 roadmap, YMYL/GDPR gates, measurement framework, decision log.
- **`docs/seo/seo-results-log.md`** (new): per-initiative status log (6-stage convention), seeded with this sprint's work.
- **`docs/seo/README.md`** (new): index disambiguating the now 5-document `docs/seo/` directory.

Rebased onto `main` after 6 unrelated HRV-sync commits landed mid-sprint (zero file overlap, clean rebase, full check suite re-run post-rebase).

## Test plan

All run locally via Docker (see repo's Docker-only policy), sequentially to avoid concurrent-build filesystem races:

- [x] `git diff --check` — clean
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` — 0 errors
- [x] `next build` — 3427 pages, exit 0 (run twice: pre-rebase and post-rebase)
- [x] `tools/check-translation-corruption.ts` — 92 files, 51913 strings, 0 leaks
- [x] `tools/check-blog-integrity.ts` — 60 posts, 0 collisions
- [x] `tools/check-llms-consistency.ts` — 0 problems (before AND after each truth fix)
- [x] `tools/check-bing-seo-recommendations.ts` — 0 problems
- [x] `scripts/check-mobile-routes.mjs` — 44 routes ok
- [x] Manual verification against a locally-built server: canonical/hreflang/robots/sitemap/JSON-LD for all `/fitness-data-sync` locales, the new article (both languages + all 9 noindex variants), the NL Bing-fix page, Garmin/Samsung redirects (single-hop 308), Organization/WebSite/MobileApplication discovery graph, no `localhost` leakage in rendered output despite a pre-existing (unrelated) `metadataBase` build warning
- [ ] Vercel preview (`fitmesh-site-nlhdfg23v-...vercel.app`) reached READY but is SSO-protected — could not curl-verify; will re-verify on the public URL immediately after this merges and deploys

## Known residual limitations (not fixed in this sprint, documented in the master plan backlog)

- `og:image` is missing site-wide (not just on `/fitness-data-sync`) — pre-existing, root-caused to Next.js file-based OG image resolution not applying beyond `blog/[slug]`, `lp/[slug]`, `sync/[provider]`. Needs a dedicated technical sprint.
- `/` redirects to `/it` rather than serving content directly at the site apex, so the `WebSite` JSON-LD's declared URL isn't itself reachable without a redirect (pre-existing, documented in `components/seo/WebSiteJsonLd.tsx`).
- 244 blog/landing titles exceed 70 characters (pre-existing); not touched this sprint beyond the 2 Bing explicitly flagged — backlogged, prioritize by GSC impressions before touching.
