items.title: Created Standalone GCS benchmark tool v1
items.body:
# PR Summary: `gcs-bench` — Standalone GCS Benchmark Tool

**Branch:** `gcs-bench-tool-v1`  
**Base:** `origin/master` (upstream snapshot `582a2201`, 2026-03-27)  
**Author:** Russ Fellows \<russ.fellows@gmail.com\>  
**Commits:** 24  

---

## Overview

This PR adds `gcs-bench`, a standalone GCS I/O benchmark tool built on top of the
`gcsfuse` internals (native GCS client, bidi-gRPC / RAPID transport, retry logic).
It is entirely additive — no existing gcsfuse code is modified except for a single
nil-guard bug fix in the retry path and one auto-generated file refresh.

The tool is designed for benchmarking GCS at line rate for AI/ML workloads, with
first-class support for RAPID (bidi-gRPC) transport verification, HDR latency
histograms, incompressible write data, and fully self-contained result directories.

---

## Commit-by-Commit Breakdown

### Foundation

#### `37188c8c` — feat: add gcs-bench standalone benchmark tool
Initial commit introducing the complete `gcs-bench` binary.

- **`cmd/` package:** `main.go` dispatcher, `benchmark.go` (primary subcommand),
  `merge.go` (`merge-results` subcommand).
- **`internal/benchmark/` package:** `config.go` (YAML config parsing), `engine.go`
  (run loop, goroutine pool, per-track I/O workers), `exporter.go` (write results to
  `.txt` / `.yaml` / `.tsv`), `histograms.go` (HDR histogram wrappers), `metrics.go`
  (atomic counters, interval snapshots), `preflight.go` (connectivity/permission
  checks), `types.go` (shared data structures).
- Config-driven: YAML file specifies object counts, sizes, concurrency, warmup /
  measurement durations, output path, and mix of read/write/stat/list tracks.
- **Makefile:** `bench`, `bench-test`, `bench-clean` targets added.

#### `c6c51ccd` — fix: correct metric collection — latency, avg op size, measured throughput
Early bug fix before any real runs were possible:
- Latency histogram was recording wall-clock nanoseconds instead of per-op duration.
- Average op size was computing objects/bytes instead of bytes/objects.
- Measured throughput was using configured object size instead of actual bytes transferred.

---

### Output Quality

#### `2d9e00d3` — feat: human-readable `.txt` output + fix TTFB reporting for writes
- `Export()` now always writes a `.txt` file alongside `.yaml`/`.tsv` — no flags needed.
- `printHumanSummary()` shared by `PrintSummary` (stdout) and `writeHumanText` (file).
- Auto-scaling units: µs when < 10,000 µs, otherwise ms (e.g. `78.53 ms`); GiB/MiB/KiB
  for sizes; comma thousands separators for integers.
- Write/stat/list tracks show `TTFB: N/A (write operation)` instead of zeros.
- Added `OpType` string field to `TrackStats` (yaml: `op_type`).

#### `dbf572fa` — docs: update bench-user-guide for human-readable output and TTFB fixes
Comprehensive documentation update to `docs/bench-user-guide.md` covering:
- Updated example output using real benchmark data.
- Corrected TTFB vs TTLB descriptions.
- Added `avg_op_size_bytes` column to TSV reference.
- Documented write-latency recording in prepare mode.

---

### Bug Fixes

#### `ba80e201` — fix: nil-guard MetricHandle in ShouldRetryWithMonitoring — prevents SIGSEGV
`gcs-bench` does not configure a `MetricHandle` in its `StorageClientConfig`. When a
bidi-gRPC stream received a throttling error, `ShouldRetryWithMonitoring` called
`metricHandle.GcsRetryCount(...)` on a nil interface → SIGSEGV.

Fix: nil-check around `GcsRetryCount`. Retry decision still computed and returned
correctly; only the (inapplicable) metric recording is skipped.

Regression test: `TestShouldRetryWithMonitoringNilMetricHandle` verifies all four
cases (nil error, non-retryable, retryable, DeadlineExceeded) with nil handle do
not panic. **This is the only change to an existing `gcsfuse` source file.**

#### `b1dcdb6b` — fix: read-size=0 reads full object; add live progress output every 10s
- `ReadSize <= 0` now leaves `req.Range = nil` → GCS returns entire object.
  Previously defaulted to a 4 MiB range read, causing partial reads and spurious
  retry storms for objects larger than 4 MiB (e.g. UNet3D lognormal distribution).
- Added `TestDoReadFullObjectWhenReadSizeIsZero` regression test.
- Background goroutine logs interval ops and GiB/s every 10 s during measurement,
  eliminating silent runs that were indistinguishable from hangs.

---

### RAPID Transport Verification & Progress Visibility

#### `6c4c328a` — feat: RAPID confirmation log; warmup+measurement 10s progress; -vv detail
- On startup, checks `bt.Zonal` and logs whether bidi-gRPC (RAPID) transport is
  **ACTIVE** or the bucket uses standard HTTP/2. Operators can now confirm RAPID is
  engaged before waiting for results.
- `Engine.verbosity` field added; `NewEngine` accepts it as a parameter.
- `startProgressReporter()` logs every 10 s for both warmup and measurement:
  - `-v`: compact interval ops + GiB/s per track.
  - `-vv`: also logs elapsed, remaining, total-ops, total-errs per track.
- `make bench` target now runs `go generate ./...` before build so
  `make clean && make bench` no longer breaks due to deleted generated files.

#### `77a6c4c8` — chore: commit regenerated cfg/ and metrics/ files from go generate
Auto-generated files missing from the preceding commit; no manual changes.

#### `3003662a` — docs: update bench-user-guide with real -v output and RAPID confirmation flow
- Added full RAPID detection sequence to the guide (timing, DirectPath check, CONFIRMED log).
- Updated verbosity table with real observed output.
- Noted that a small DeadlineExceeded burst at phase boundaries is normal.

#### `1efba0cc` — feat: progress always visible by default; add HDR `.hgrm` histogram output
- Progress ticks switched from `logger.Infof` (requires `-v`) to `fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr)`
  — always visible without any flags.
- `histograms.go`: `WritePercentileDistribution(ttfbW, totalW io.Writer)` using
  `PercentilesPrint` with 5 ticks/half and 1000× scale (µs → ms).
- `engine.go`: `Histograms() []*TrackHistograms` accessor.
- `exporter.go`: `ExportHgrm()` writes two `.hgrm` files per track (TTFB + total latency).
- Compatible with [HdrHistogram plot page](https://hdrhistogram.github.io/HdrHistogram/plotFiles.html).

---

### Data Generation (Incompressible Writes)

#### `6cd59c9c` — feat: Xoshiro256++ write data generation with lock-free producer/consumer pipeline
Rewrites the write-data path completely. Previous `make([]byte, size)` produced
all-zero buffers — maximally compressible and deduplicated at the storage layer,
making write benchmarks meaningless on systems with inline compression (e.g. RAPID).

Three-layer pipeline:

1. **`datagen.go` — Xoshiro256++ PRNG:** Same generator as `dgen-rs`
   (`rand_xoshiro::Xoshiro256PlusPlus`). Each 1 MiB block uses a unique seed
   (entropy + monotonic sequence counter) so no two blocks share RNG state.
   Parallel goroutine fill matches dgen-rs's `rayon::par_chunks_mut` path.

2. **`datapool.go` — Lock-free ring buffer:** Fixed-size ring of pre-allocated
   write buffers. Single producer goroutine fills slots; consumer goroutines
   (doWrite workers) acquire pre-filled slots, stream to GCS, release.
   Slot state machine (`EMPTY → FILLING → READY → CONSUMING → EMPTY`) controlled
   by one `atomic.Uint32` per slot, padded to its own 64-byte cache line to
   eliminate false sharing.

3. **Engine integration:** `Engine.writePool *DataPool` created in `NewEngine`.
   `doWrite` fast path: `AcquireSlot → stream → ReleaseSlot`. Zero heap allocation,
   zero inline fill in the hot path. Inline fallback when pool is nil or object
   size exceeds pool capacity (>512 MiB).

4. **`datagen-bench` subcommand:** Measures raw Xoshiro256++ throughput at
   `GOMAXPROCS = 1, 2, 4, 8, …, NumCPU`. Observed on 12-core Xeon Platinum 8280L:
   20.83 GB/s at full concurrency (≥1.5× headroom over 12 GiB/s network rate).

#### `77463e3d` — fix: gofmt indentation in datapool.go; confirm 64 MiB outer buffer
- `gofmt` canonical four-space indent applied to block-comment parameter list.
- Empirically validated 64 MiB outer buffer: at 12 cores (full benchmark load),
  64 MiB yields 21.25 GB/s vs 20.51 GB/s for 32 MiB — justified by dgen-rs
  benchmarks on smaller systems showing the opposite, which reverses at high
  concurrency on the target hardware.

#### `470ce67b` — feat: DataPool produce/consume telemetry with periodic reporting and final summary
Instrumentation to detect if data generation is the write bottleneck.

Four atomic counters added to `DataPool`:
- `bytesProduced` / `bytesConsumed`: monotonically increasing byte counters.
- `producerStallNs` / `consumerStallNs`: goroutine-ns waiting for EMPTY / READY slots.

Periodic report (every 10 s at `-v`):
```
[pool] produce=X.XX GiB/s  consume=X.XX GiB/s  ratio=X.XXX
       producer-stall=X.XX%  consumer-stall=X.XX%
```
If `produce/consume ratio < 1.05`, a WARNING is emitted at any verbosity level.
Final summary logged after measurement completes. Overhead is O(1 clock read per
yield), negligible vs GCS upload latency.

---

### Concurrency Tracking

#### `d2c40219` — feat: record and report goroutine (thread) count per track in all output formats
The goroutine count per track was visible in dry-run console output but absent from
result files, making it impossible to correlate results to concurrency settings after
the fact.

- `TrackStats.Goroutines int` field added (yaml: `goroutines`).
- `.txt`: `Threads: N goroutines` line added below track header.
- `.yaml`: marshals automatically.
- `.tsv`: `goroutines` column added as second column (after `track`).
- `merge.go`: propagated from `workers[0].Tracks[i]` in merged output.

---

### Output Organization

#### `6f620ebd` — fix: suppress phase-transition DeadlineExceeded noise; collect outputs in subdirectory

**Issue 1 — Noisy phase transitions:**  
At warmup→measurement and end-of-measurement, in-flight gRPC calls surface as
`DeadlineExceeded` errors and were being logged twice (retry path + engine worker).
Fix: skip the `Warnf` in `ShouldRetry` when gRPC code is `DeadlineExceeded` or
`Canceled`; check `ctx.Err() != nil` in `runWorker` before counting / logging errors.
Genuine GCS errors are still counted and logged.

**Issue 2 — Consolidated output directory:**  
Flat file layout changed to timestamped subdirectory:
```
results/bench-20260329-225301/
    bench.txt
    bench.yaml
    bench.tsv
    unet3d-read-ttfb.hgrm
    unet3d-read-total-latency.hgrm
```

#### `8908d4c7` — feat: copy config into results directory; update docs for new output layout
- `ExportConfig()` copies the benchmark YAML into `config.yaml` inside the result
  subdirectory. Every result directory is now fully self-contained.
- `bench-user-guide.md` updated throughout to show the current directory tree.

---

### Warmup Correctness

#### `a6d4b892` — refactor: single goroutine pool through warmup+measurement phases
The original implementation called `runPhase()` twice with separate contexts —
warmup context cancelled → goroutine teardown → stat reset → respawn for measurement.
This caused a visible gap in progress output and spurious `DeadlineExceeded` errors.

Replacement:
- Single `runCtx` with timeout = `WarmupDuration + Duration`.
- I/O goroutines spin up once and run through both phases without interruption.
- `time.After(WarmupDuration)` fires; stats reset atomically (`Store(0)` + `hists.Reset()`).
- No context cancellation at the phase boundary. Dead `runPhase()` helper removed.

---

### Console Log Capture

#### `d5bd58a9` — feat: capture console output to console.log in results directory
All terminal output during a run is now also saved to `console.log` in the result
subdirectory, making each result directory fully self-contained for sharing / archiving.

Implementation:
- `Engine.out io.Writer` field (defaults to `os.Stderr`).
- `RunPreflight`, `Export`, `ExportHgrm`, `ExportConfig`, `PrintSummary` all accept
  an `io.Writer` for console output.
- `cmd/benchmark.go` creates:
  ```go
  consoleOut  = io.MultiWriter(os.Stdout, &logBuf)
  progressOut = io.MultiWriter(os.Stderr, &logBuf)
  ```
  After all exports, `ExportConsoleLog(summary, outputPath, logBuf.Bytes())` writes
  the captured bytes to `console.log`.

**Final result directory layout:**
```
results/bench-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS/
    bench.txt               ← human-readable summary
    bench.yaml              ← machine-readable metrics
    bench.tsv               ← TSV for spreadsheet import
    config.yaml             ← exact config used (reproducibility)
    <track>-ttfb.hgrm       ← HDR histogram (TTFB, reads only)
    <track>-total-latency.hgrm  ← HDR histogram (end-to-end)
    console.log             ← full terminal output
```

---

### Version String

#### `e5708510` — build: inject gcs-bench version via -ldflags at build time
Adds `BENCH_VERSION` variable (default: `v1.0`) injected via `-ldflags` into
`common.gcsfuseVersion`. `--version` now reports a useful string instead of `unknown`.

#### `e1166ad3` — build: encode upstream snapshot SHA in version string
`UPSTREAM_SHA` computed automatically from `git merge-base HEAD origin/master`.  
`--version` output:
```
gcsfuse version gcsfuse-v3-snap.582a2201+bench-v1.0 (Go version go1.26.1)
```
- `gcsfuse-v3` — upstream codebase generation
- `snap.582a2201` — short SHA of the exact upstream commit this fork tracks
- `+bench-v1.0` — benchmark tool revision (bump with `make bench BENCH_VERSION=vX.Y`)

---

### SVG Histogram Plotting

#### `150a8a11` — feat: add plot-hgrm subcommand with log/linear scale SVG output
New `gcs-bench plot-hgrm` subcommand:
- Reads one or more `.hgrm` HDR histogram files.
- Generates self-contained SVG frequency distribution chart.
- Log-scale X axis (default): symmetric bell curve for lognormal latency data.
- `--scale linear` for narrow distributions.
- Multi-file overlay with colour-coded legend.
- Zero new dependencies (pure stdlib SVG generation).

---

### Documentation & Housekeeping

#### `bed348fe` — docs: replace README.md with benchmark-focused top-level page
- `git mv README.md README-gcsfuse-upstream.md` — upstream gcsfuse content preserved
  with history.
- New `README.md` focused on `gcs-bench`: quick-start, Make targets, subcommands
  table, documentation index, key features, pointer to upstream README.

#### `8cf6ce27` — build: gitignore gcs-bench binary; fix metrics_test.go alignment
#### `534f8148` — build: add bench/bench-test/bench-clean Makefile targets

---

## Files Added (new to this branch)

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `cmd/benchmark.go` | `bench` subcommand entry point |
| `cmd/datagen_bench.go` | `datagen-bench` throughput measurement subcommand |
| `cmd/merge.go` | `merge-results` subcommand |
| `cmd/plot.go` | `plot-hgrm` SVG generation subcommand |
| `internal/benchmark/config.go` | YAML config parsing |
| `internal/benchmark/datagen.go` | Xoshiro256++ PRNG implementation |
| `internal/benchmark/datapool.go` | Lock-free ring buffer for write data |
| `internal/benchmark/engine.go` | Core benchmark engine |
| `internal/benchmark/exporter.go` | Result file writer (txt/yaml/tsv/hgrm/console.log) |
| `internal/benchmark/histograms.go` | HDR histogram wrappers |
| `internal/benchmark/metrics.go` | Atomic counters, interval snapshots |
| `internal/benchmark/preflight.go` | Pre-flight connectivity checks |
| `internal/benchmark/types.go` | Shared type definitions |
| `internal/benchmark/*_test.go` | Unit tests for all components |
| `docs/bench-user-guide.md` | Full user guide |
| `docs/Handoff_gcsfuse-bench.md` | Handoff / architectural rationale |
| `README.md` | Benchmark-focused top-level README |
| `README-gcsfuse-upstream.md` | Original gcsfuse README (renamed) |

## Files Modified (existing gcsfuse code)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `internal/storage/storageutil/custom_retry.go` | nil-guard on `MetricHandle` (SIGSEGV fix) |
| `Makefile` | Added `bench` / `bench-test` / `bench-clean` targets, ldflags |
| `.gitignore` | Added `gcs-bench` binary |
| `main.go` | Dispatch to new subcommands |

---

## Testing

All existing gcsfuse tests continue to pass. New tests added:
- `TestShouldRetryWithMonitoringNilMetricHandle` (nil MetricHandle SIGSEGV regression)
- `TestDoReadFullObjectWhenReadSizeIsZero` (read-size=0 regression)
- Engine, exporter, metrics, histogram, datapool unit tests

```bash
GOTOOLCHAIN=auto go test ./internal/benchmark/... -v   # all pass
GOTOOLCHAIN=auto go test ./internal/storage/...        # unmodified, all pass
```

items.body:
# Pull Request: Memory Protection Unit (MPU) Implementation

**Branch:** `feature/mpu-protection` → `dev`  
**Author:** Souham Biswas (@ironhide23586)  
**Date Range:** February 2, 2026 - March 22, 2026  
**Commits:** 44 commits  
**Files Changed:** 86 files (+14,838 / -10,014 lines)  
**Status:** ✅ Ready for Review

---

## Executive Summary

This PR implements comprehensive hardware-enforced memory protection for Icarus OS using the ARM Cortex-M7 Memory Protection Unit (MPU). The implementation provides three layers of isolation:

1. **DTCM Protection** - Kernel data structures isolated in privileged-only memory
2. **ITCM Protection** - Kernel code marked read-only to prevent modification attacks
3. **Task Data Isolation** - Each task gets an isolated 2KB data region, preventing cross-task corruption

The journey involved 44 commits over 7 weeks, with significant architectural learnings, multiple design pivots, and comprehensive verification. All 131 unit tests pass, and 5 new MPU-specific stress tests validate the protection mechanisms.

---

## Table of Contents

1. [Feature Overview](#feature-overview)
2. [Architecture](#architecture)
3. [The Journey: Commit-by-Commit Analysis](#the-journey)
4. [Key Learnings](#key-learnings)
5. [Challenges & Solutions](#challenges--solutions)
6. [Verification & Testing](#verification--testing)
7. [DO-178C Documentation](#do-178c-documentation)
8. [Performance Impact](#performance-impact)
9. [Breaking Changes](#breaking-changes)
10. [Future Work](#future-work)

---

## Feature Overview

### What This PR Delivers


**Hardware-Enforced Memory Protection:**
- ✅ Kernel data (task lists, semaphores, pipes, tick counter) isolated in privileged-only DTCM
- ✅ Kernel code marked read-only in ITCM (prevents code modification attacks)
- ✅ Per-task 2KB data regions with MPU reconfiguration on context switch
- ✅ Tasks run in unprivileged mode (CONTROL.nPRIV=1)
- ✅ Kernel functions run in privileged mode via SVC call gates

**SVC Call Gate Architecture:**
- 39 SVC numbers defined for controlled privilege transitions
- 11 new SVC call gates (SVCs 29-39) for atomic kernel state access
- Spinning functions (semaphore feed/consume, pipe enqueue/dequeue) use call gates to read DTCM

**Fault Handling:**
- Graceful recovery from MemManage faults (data access violations)
- Fault address and PC captured for debugging
- System remains stable after intentional attack tests

**Verification:**
- 5 new MPU attack test tasks (red team testing)
- 131 unit tests pass (0 failures)
- Comprehensive stress testing under high contention
- DO-178C documentation updated with 14 new memory protection requirements

---

## Architecture

### MPU Region Configuration

The implementation uses 8 MPU regions on ARM Cortex-M7:

| Region | Base Address | Size | Access | Purpose |
|--------|--------------|------|--------|---------|
| **0** | 0x00000000 | 64KB | Priv+User RO+Exec | ITCM code (kernel handlers) |
| **1** | 0x90000000 | 8MB | Priv+User RO+Exec | QSPI Flash (external) |
| **2** | 0x08000000 | 128KB | Priv+User RO+Exec | Internal Flash |
| **3** | DISABLED | - | - | Reserved (consolidated with Region 0) |
| **4** | Dynamic | 2KB | Priv+User RW | Task data (reconfigured per context switch) |
| **5** | 0x20000000 | 128KB | **Priv RW only** | DTCM (kernel data - **PROTECTED**) |
| **6** | 0x24000000 | 512KB | Priv+User Full | RAM_D1 (stacks, shared buffers) |
| **7** | 0x40000000 | 512MB | Priv+User Device | Peripherals (GPIO, USB, etc.) |

**Key Protection Mechanisms:**

1. **DTCM Protection (Region 5):**
   - Kernel state (task_list, semaphore_list, message_pipe_list, os_tick_count) isolated
   - Unprivileged tasks cannot directly read/write kernel data
   - All kernel data access forced through SVC call gates

2. **ITCM Protection (Region 0):**
   - Kernel code read-only for all (prevents code modification attacks)
   - ARM exception architecture prevents unprivileged execution of privileged handlers

3. **Task Data Isolation (Region 4):**
   - Each task allocated 2KB data region (ICARUS_DATA_WORDS = 512 words)
   - MPU Region 4 reconfigured on every context switch
   - Prevents cross-task memory corruption

### SVC Call Gate Architecture

**Problem:** Once DTCM is privileged-only, spinning functions (semaphore feed/consume, pipe enqueue/dequeue) cannot read kernel state (count, max_count, engaged flags) from unprivileged mode.

**Solution:** SVC call gates that read/write kernel state atomically in privileged mode:

**Read Gates (SVCs 29-32, 37-39):**
- `SVC_SEM_CAN_FEED` - Check if semaphore can accept feed
- `SVC_SEM_CAN_CONSUME` - Check if semaphore can be consumed
- `SVC_PIPE_CAN_ENQUEUE` - Check if pipe has room
- `SVC_PIPE_CAN_DEQUEUE` - Check if pipe has data
- `SVC_OS_GET_TICK_COUNT` - Read os_tick_count for busy-wait loops
- `SVC_OS_GET_TASK_NAME` - Read task name for display
- `SVC_OS_GET_NUM_CREATED_TASKS` - Read task count for display

**Write Gates (SVCs 33-36):**
- `SVC_SEM_INCREMENT` - Increment semaphore count atomically
- `SVC_SEM_DECREMENT` - Decrement semaphore count atomically
- `SVC_PIPE_WRITE_BYTES` - Write to pipe buffer atomically
- `SVC_PIPE_READ_BYTES` - Read from pipe buffer atomically

**Spinning Pattern:**
```c
bool semaphore_feed(uint8_t semaphore_idx) {
    while (!sem_can_feed(semaphore_idx)) {  // SVC call gate
        task_active_sleep(1);
    }
    sem_increment(semaphore_idx);  // SVC write gate
    return true;
}
```

---

## The Journey: Commit-by-Commit Analysis

### Phase 1: Foundation & Refactoring (Feb 2-6, 2026) - 10 commits

**Goal:** Prepare codebase for MPU implementation by modularizing the monolithic kernel.


#### Commit 1: `fb0e8d9` - BSP header cleanup and MPU foundation
- Removed `bsp_` prefix from all BSP headers (bsp_gpio.h → gpio.h)
- Added skeleton `bsp/mpu.h` and `bsp/mpu.c`
- Moved pin definitions from main.h to bsp/config.h
- **Learning:** Clean header structure essential before adding complexity

#### Commits 2-3: `505e6b1`, `bfdb386` - Kernel modularization
- Split monolithic `icarus_task.c` (1729 lines) into modular components:
  - `kernel.c` - Core kernel state and initialization
  - `task.c` - Task lifecycle management
  - `scheduler.c` - Scheduling and timing services
  - `semaphore.c` - Semaphore operations
  - `pipe.c` - Message pipe operations
- Created umbrella header `icarus/icarus.h` replacing `icarus_task.h`
- **Learning:** Modular structure makes privilege separation clearer

#### Commits 4-6: `41f04f1`, `a823d25`, `b1de983` - MPU configuration and test fixes
- Added explicit VTOR configuration for interrupt vector table
- Defined 8 MPU regions with proper memory attributes
- Fixed test build issues and mock system
- **Learning:** Test infrastructure must evolve with production code

#### Commits 7-10: `5f6f411`, `5ccd110`, `a2eaeb6`, `0ac33aa` - Task data isolation
- Implemented per-task 2KB data regions in RAM_D2 (2KB-aligned)
- Added `MPU_ConfigureTaskData()` called from context switch handler
- Created `kernel_alloc_task_data()` for runtime allocation within task regions
- Added MPU verification tasks to stress test
- **Stats:** +500 lines in mpu.c, context_switch.s, kernel.c
- **Learning:** Dynamic MPU reconfiguration works! Context switch overhead acceptable (~2μs)

**Phase 1 Summary:** Foundation laid. Task data isolation working. DTCM/ITCM protection deferred.

---

### Phase 2: Privilege Separation Refactoring (Mar 1-2, 2026) - 13 commits

**Goal:** Separate privileged kernel functions from unprivileged wrappers using SVC mechanism.


#### Commit 11: `7820f53` - Enhanced MPU verification with red team testing
- Added `mpu_redteam_task` that attempts cross-task memory access
- Added `mpu_verify_task` with multiple allocations and pattern integrity checks
- **Learning:** Need intentional attack tests to validate protection

#### Commit 12: `1f4649f` - Step 1: Safe refactoring
- Added `svc.h` with initial SVC number defines
- Added MPU attack test code with `MPU_ENABLE_ATTACK_TEST=0` (disabled)
- Added retarget_hal mock for host testing
- **Learning:** Incremental approach essential - don't break working system

#### Commit 13: `c9ffaac` - Step 2: Rename privileged functions with `__` prefix
- Renamed all kernel functions: `os_init()` → `__os_init()`
- Created public wrappers: `void os_init(void) { __os_init(); }`
- **Stats:** 50+ function renames across kernel.c, task.c, scheduler.c, semaphore.c, pipe.c
- **Learning:** Naming convention makes privilege boundary explicit

#### Commit 14: `8fd03d4` - Step 3a: Complete `__` prefix renaming
- Completed renaming for all public API functions
- Assigned full SVC numbers (0-39)
- Cleaned up queue logic in pipe.c
- **Learning:** Consistent naming prevents confusion during SVC implementation

#### Commit 15: `939f2e9` - Step 3b: Move all public wrappers to svc.c
- Created `svc.c` with inline assembly SVC wrappers
- Example: `void enter_critical(void) { __asm__ volatile ("svc %0\n" : : "I" (SVC_ENTER_CRITICAL)); }`
- **Stats:** +600 lines in svc.c
- **Learning:** Centralized SVC wrappers easier to maintain than scattered across files

#### Commit 16: `a1185b2` - Step 3c: Direct-call wrappers (debugging)
- Temporarily disabled SVC dispatch for debugging
- Wrappers call `__func()` directly instead of issuing SVC
- **Learning:** Incremental testing - verify logic before adding SVC complexity

#### Commit 17: `bf46fc7` - Step 3c: Enable SVC dispatch for critical sections
- Enabled SVC dispatch for `enter_critical()`, `exit_critical()`, `os_yield()`
- Added getter SVCs for task metadata
- **Learning:** Start with simple SVCs before complex ones

#### Commits 18-19: `d1e8773`, `533d6de` - Step 3d-3e: SVC dispatch for all wrappers
- Enabled SVC dispatch for all non-spinning wrappers
- Created thread-mode wrappers for spinning functions (semaphore feed/consume, pipe enqueue/dequeue)
- **Learning:** Spinning functions cannot run in SVC handler (PendSV lower priority)

#### Commit 20: `36cf42c` - Step 3f: MPU regions for unprivileged task execution
- Set CONTROL=0x03 in context_switch.s (unprivileged + PSP)
- Configured MPU with privileged default background map
- **Stats:** Tasks now run unprivileged! Major milestone.
- **Learning:** Privileged default background blocks unprivileged access to system control space

#### Commits 21-23: `65397fb`, `ace7b93` - Step 3g: Cleanup and style
- Removed duplicate spinning implementations from svc.c
- Applied VxWorks K&R style to all kernel files
- **Learning:** Code style consistency matters for certification

**Phase 2 Summary:** Privilege separation complete. Tasks run unprivileged. SVC mechanism working.

---

### Phase 3: Memory Section Placement (Mar 1-2, 2026) - 6 commits

**Goal:** Place kernel code/data in ITCM/DTCM with linker script and section attributes.


#### Commit 24: `4d08693` - Step 4: Section placement macros
- Added `ITCM_FUNC_PRIV`, `ITCM_FUNC`, `DTCM_DATA_PRIV` macros in config.h
- Example: `#define ITCM_FUNC_PRIV __attribute__((section(".itcm_priv")))`
- **Learning:** Macros make section placement explicit and searchable

#### Commit 25: `594a59b` - Step 5: Linker script split
- Split ITCM into `.itcm_priv` (1KB) and `.itcm_user` (63KB)
- Split DTCM into `.dtcm_priv` (kernel data) and `.dtcm_user` (unused)
- Updated startup code to copy sections from flash to ITCM/DTCM
- **Stats:** 100+ lines in linker script changes
- **Learning:** Linker script complexity increases with fine-grained sections

#### Commits 26-28: `aac649f`, `ce236b1`, `3a6daf3` - Step 6: ITCM_PRIV MPU region
- Configured MPU Region 3 for ITCM_PRIV (1KB, privileged-only)
- Used subregion disable (0xFC) to protect only first 256 bytes
- Fixed alignment issues (.itcm_user must be 1KB-aligned)
- **Learning:** MPU subregion disable allows fine-grained protection within regions

#### Commit 29: `eeabbc3` - Added steering docs
- Documented project context and MPU architecture learnings
- Created `.kiro/steering/` documentation for team knowledge sharing
- **Learning:** Document architectural decisions while fresh in mind

#### Commits 30-31: `9ad00e8`, `b1511ba` - Step 7a: ITCM attack test and SVC call gates
- Added `mpu_itcm_priv_attack_task` that attempts ITCM write
- Implemented recoverable MemManage handler with fault address capture
- Added initial SVC call gates for spinning functions
- **Learning:** Fault recovery essential for graceful degradation

**Phase 3 Summary:** Memory sections placed. ITCM_PRIV region configured. Attack tests added.

---

### Phase 4: DTCM Protection & Debugging (Mar 20-21, 2026) - 12 commits

**Goal:** Enable DTCM protection and fix all resulting access violations.


#### Commit 32: `ded7caa` - Step 7b: DTCM protection with SVC call gates
- **THE BIG ONE:** Enabled DTCM protection (Region 5: PRIV_RW)
- Added 11 SVC call gates (SVCs 29-39) for atomic kernel state access
- Moved all privileged functions to ITCM_PRIV section
- Updated display.c to use SVC wrappers for task metadata
- Enhanced MemManage handler with fault loop detection (limit: 1000 faults)
- **Stats:** +400 lines in svc.c, +100 lines in stm32h7xx_it.c
- **Learning:** DTCM protection requires comprehensive SVC coverage

#### Commit 33: `5d6fa2b` - Fix DTCM access in display_init
- **Bug:** display_init() was reading task names directly from DTCM
- **Fix:** Copy task names to RAM_D1 buffer before display
- **Learning:** Every DTCM access must be audited and wrapped

#### Commits 34-35: `301b975`, `42a2d6d` - Printf mutex experiments
- Added printf mutex for serialization (caused deadlock)
- Removed printf mutex, simplified display_init
- **Learning:** Mutex in display code can deadlock with scheduler

#### Commit 36: `758b50c` - Add os_is_running() SVC wrapper
- **Bug:** Heartbeat task was reading `os_running` flag from DTCM
- **Fix:** Added `SVC_OS_IS_RUNNING` call gate
- **Learning:** Global flags in DTCM need SVC wrappers

#### Commit 37: `47aa9c6` - Fix USB enumeration timing
- **Bug:** USB enumeration failing after DTCM protection enabled
- **Fix:** Adjusted timing in USB initialization
- **Learning:** DTCM protection can expose timing-sensitive bugs

#### Commit 38: `cbe4644` - Enable DTCM protection with task name buffer fix
- Fixed task name buffer allocation in display.c
- DTCM protection now stable with all demo tasks running
- **Learning:** Buffer management critical when crossing privilege boundaries

#### Commit 39: `3c722ab` - DTCM protection working, ITCM_PRIV deferred
- DTCM protection fully working with all stress tests passing
- ITCM_PRIV region causing library code faults (deferred investigation)
- **Learning:** Prioritize working features over perfect architecture

#### Commit 40: `c21b252` - Enable DTCM protection and all stress tests
- All 19 stress test tasks running with DTCM protection
- MPU attack tests validating protection mechanisms
- **Stats:** 0 faults during normal operation, intentional attacks caught
- **Learning:** Comprehensive stress testing validates protection

**Phase 4 Summary:** DTCM protection working! All stress tests pass. System stable.

---

### Phase 5: Consolidation & Documentation (Mar 21-22, 2026) - 5 commits

**Goal:** Simplify architecture and complete DO-178C documentation.


#### Commit 41: `ae6231e` - Fix MPU task data isolation
- **Bug:** Task data isolation test failing intermittently
- **Fix:** Added memory barriers (DSB/ISB) after MPU reconfiguration
- Corrected test logic for pattern verification
- **Learning:** Memory barriers essential for MPU changes to take effect

#### Commit 42: `3fd21be` - Consolidate ITCM sections
- **Major Simplification:** Removed ITCM_PRIV/USER split
- Merged into single `.itcm` section with Region 0 (RO for all)
- Disabled MPU Region 3 (ITCM_PRIV) - provides no additional security
- **Rationale:** ARM exception architecture already protects kernel handlers
- **Stats:** -100 lines in linker script, -50 lines in startup code
- **Learning:** Simpler is better. ITCM_PRIV was architectural gold-plating.

#### Commit 43: `0e866a3` - Add ITCM write protection test
- Added `mpu_itcm_write_test` that attempts ITCM write (should fault)
- Improved MemManage handler with better fault reporting
- **Learning:** Test all protection mechanisms, not just DTCM

#### Commit 44: `bc83a1e` - Complete MPU protection with DO-178C docs
- Updated SRS.md with 14 new memory protection requirements (HLR-KRN-063 to HLR-KRN-086)
- Updated SDD.md with MPU architecture section
- Updated SVP.md with MPU verification approach
- Updated coverage_analysis.md (88.5% line coverage, 85.9% function coverage)
- Updated test_traceability.md with requirements-to-test mapping
- **Stats:** +500 lines in DO-178C documentation
- **Learning:** Documentation is part of the feature, not an afterthought

#### Commit 45: `df62a0d` - Update build reports
- Regenerated cppcheck reports (clean, 0 warnings)
- Updated build artifacts
- **Learning:** Clean static analysis essential for certification

**Phase 5 Summary:** Architecture simplified. Documentation complete. Ready for review.

---

## Key Learnings

### 1. Incremental Approach is Essential
- 44 commits over 7 weeks, each commit buildable and testable
- Avoided "big bang" integration that would have been impossible to debug
- Step-by-step privilege separation (Steps 1-7) allowed validation at each stage

### 2. ARM Exception Architecture Provides Implicit Protection
- ITCM_PRIV region was unnecessary - ARM already prevents unprivileged execution of SVC/PendSV handlers
- Simplified architecture by removing ITCM_PRIV/USER split (commit `3fd21be`)
- **Lesson:** Understand hardware capabilities before adding software complexity

### 3. Spinning Functions Cannot Run in SVC Handler
- Semaphore feed/consume and pipe enqueue/dequeue are spin-wait loops
- PendSV (context switch) has lower priority than SVC - cannot preempt
- **Solution:** Spinning functions call `__func()` directly in thread mode, use SVC call gates to read DTCM
- **Lesson:** Exception priority hierarchy matters for real-time systems


### 4. Memory Barriers are Critical for MPU Reconfiguration
- Initial task data isolation test failed intermittently
- **Root Cause:** MPU changes not taking effect before task resumed
- **Fix:** Added DSB (Data Synchronization Barrier) and ISB (Instruction Synchronization Barrier)
- **Lesson:** ARM Cortex-M7 has instruction pipeline - barriers ensure ordering

### 5. Every DTCM Access Must Be Audited
- Enabling DTCM protection exposed hidden dependencies:
  - display_init() reading task names
  - Heartbeat task reading os_running flag
  - USB initialization timing
- **Solution:** Systematic audit of all DTCM accesses, wrap with SVC call gates
- **Lesson:** Protection mechanisms expose architectural assumptions

### 6. Fault Recovery Enables Graceful Degradation
- MemManage handler captures fault address and PC
- Skips faulting instruction (+2 bytes) to allow system to continue
- Fault counter prevents infinite loops (limit: 1000 faults)
- **Lesson:** Safety-critical systems need graceful degradation, not just crash-and-burn

### 7. Test Infrastructure Must Evolve with Production Code
- Added 5 new MPU attack test tasks
- Enhanced stress tests with pattern verification
- Created mock system for host testing
- **Lesson:** Verification is part of the feature, not separate

### 8. Documentation is Part of the Feature
- Updated 6 DO-178C documents with MPU requirements and architecture
- Added steering docs for team knowledge sharing
- Created FAULT_BLINK_DECODER.md for debugging
- **Lesson:** Undocumented features are incomplete features

### 9. Simpler is Better
- ITCM_PRIV region removed after realizing it provided no additional security
- Printf mutex removed after causing deadlock
- **Lesson:** Question every architectural decision - complexity is a liability

### 10. Red Team Testing Validates Protection
- MPU attack tests intentionally violate protection boundaries
- Fault counters prove protection is working
- System remains stable after attacks
- **Lesson:** Security features must be tested adversarially

---

## Challenges & Solutions

### Challenge 1: ITCM_PRIV Region Causing Library Code Faults

**Problem:** After enabling MPU Region 3 (ITCM_PRIV, privileged-only), system faulted on library code reads from ITCM padding area.

**Root Cause:** C library code (memcpy, etc.) may read from linker padding area in unprivileged mode. ITCM_PRIV region blocked these reads.

**Solution 1 (Attempted):** Used subregion disable (0xFC) to protect only first 256 bytes where kernel handlers live.

**Solution 2 (Final):** Removed ITCM_PRIV region entirely. ARM exception architecture already prevents unprivileged execution of privileged handlers. ITCM protection via Region 0 (RO for all) prevents code modification attacks.

**Commits:** `ce236b1`, `3a6daf3`, `3fd21be`

**Learning:** Hardware provides implicit protection - don't add redundant software layers.

---

### Challenge 2: Spinning Functions Need DTCM Access

**Problem:** Semaphore feed/consume and pipe enqueue/dequeue are spin-wait loops that check kernel state (count, max_count, engaged) in DTCM. Once DTCM is privileged-only, unprivileged tasks cannot read it.

**Attempted Solution 1:** Run spinning functions in SVC handler.
- **Failed:** PendSV (context switch) has lower priority than SVC - cannot preempt. Spinning in SVC handler blocks scheduler.

**Attempted Solution 2:** Raise PendSV priority above SVC.
- **Failed:** Violates ARM exception model - SVC must be higher priority for privilege escalation.

**Final Solution:** Spinning functions call `__func()` directly in thread mode. Use SVC call gates to read/write DTCM atomically:
- Read gates: `sem_can_feed()`, `sem_can_consume()`, `pipe_can_enqueue()`, `pipe_can_dequeue()`
- Write gates: `sem_increment()`, `sem_decrement()`, `pipe_write_bytes()`, `pipe_read_bytes()`

**Commits:** `b1511ba`, `ded7caa`

**Learning:** Exception priority hierarchy is fixed - work with it, not against it.

---

### Challenge 3: Display Code Reading Task Names from DTCM

**Problem:** `display_init()` was iterating through `task_list[]` in DTCM to read task names for display. Faulted after DTCM protection enabled.

**Attempted Solution 1:** Add SVC wrapper for each task name read.
- **Problem:** Would require N SVC calls for N tasks - inefficient.

**Final Solution:** Copy all task names to RAM_D1 buffer in one SVC call, then display from buffer.

```c
// In display.c
char task_names[ICARUS_MAX_TASKS][ICARUS_MAX_TASK_NAME_LEN];
uint8_t num_tasks = os_get_num_created_tasks();  // SVC call
for (uint8_t i = 0; i < num_tasks; i++) {
    const char *name = os_get_task_name(i);  // SVC call
    strncpy(task_names[i], name, ICARUS_MAX_TASK_NAME_LEN);
}
```

**Commits:** `5d6fa2b`, `cbe4644`

**Learning:** Batch SVC calls when possible to reduce overhead.

---

### Challenge 4: USB Enumeration Timing After DTCM Protection

**Problem:** USB enumeration failing intermittently after DTCM protection enabled.

**Root Cause:** SVC call overhead changed timing of USB initialization sequence. USB host expects responses within tight timing windows.

**Solution:** Adjusted timing in USB initialization to account for SVC overhead.

**Commit:** `47aa9c6`

**Learning:** Protection mechanisms can expose timing-sensitive bugs. Real-time systems need timing analysis.

---

### Challenge 5: Printf Mutex Deadlock

**Problem:** Added mutex to serialize printf calls from multiple tasks. System deadlocked.

**Root Cause:** Display code calls printf while holding scheduler lock. If another task holds printf mutex, deadlock occurs.

**Solution:** Removed printf mutex. Display code already runs in critical section (scheduler disabled).

**Commits:** `301b975`, `42a2d6d`

**Learning:** Mutexes in display/logging code are dangerous. Use lock-free logging or single-writer pattern.

---

### Challenge 6: Task Data Isolation Test Intermittent Failures

**Problem:** MPU task data isolation test failing intermittently - red team task sometimes successfully corrupted victim task data.

**Root Cause:** MPU reconfiguration in context switch not taking effect before task resumed. ARM Cortex-M7 instruction pipeline can execute stale MPU configuration.

**Solution:** Added memory barriers after MPU reconfiguration:

```asm
bl      MPU_ConfigureTaskData      /* Reconfigure MPU Region 4 */
dsb                                 /* Data Synchronization Barrier */
isb                                 /* Instruction Synchronization Barrier */
```

**Commit:** `ae6231e`

**Learning:** Memory barriers are not optional for MPU changes - they are required by ARM architecture.

---

### Challenge 7: Heartbeat Task Reading os_running Flag

**Problem:** Heartbeat task faulted after DTCM protection enabled - was reading `os_running` flag directly from DTCM.

**Solution:** Added `SVC_OS_IS_RUNNING` call gate:

```c
bool os_is_running(void) {
    uint32_t result;
    __asm__ volatile (
        "svc %1\n"
        "mov %0, r0\n"
        : "=r" (result)
        : "I" (SVC_OS_IS_RUNNING)
        : "r0"
    );
    return (bool)result;
}
```

**Commit:** `758b50c`

**Learning:** Global flags in DTCM need SVC wrappers. Audit all global variable accesses.

---

## Verification & Testing

### Unit Tests

**Status:** ✅ 131 tests pass, 0 failures

**Coverage:**
- Line coverage: 88.5%
- Function coverage: 85.9%
- Branch coverage: 82.3%

**Test Categories:**
- Task lifecycle (creation, termination, suicide, kill)
- Semaphore operations (feed, consume, overflow, underflow)
- Pipe operations (enqueue, dequeue, variable sizes)
- Scheduler (yield, sleep, tick counting)
- Kernel data protection (SVC call gates)


### Stress Tests

**19 Total Stress Test Tasks:**

1. **Semaphore Stress (7 tasks):**
   - `sem_hammer_fast_0/1` - Rapid feed/consume bursts (1000 ops/burst)
   - `sem_stress_med_0/1` - Adaptive medium-speed operations
   - `sem_stress_slow` - Pattern-based slow operations
   - `sem_mutex_stress_0/1` - Binary semaphore (mutex) stress

2. **Pipe Stress (8 tasks):**
   - `pipe_flood_sender/receiver` - Maximum throughput with backpressure
   - `pipe_multi_prod_0/1/2` + `pipe_multi_cons` - Multiple producers, single consumer
   - `pipe_varsz_sender/receiver` - Variable message sizes (1, 2, 4, 8 bytes)

3. **Scheduler Stress (3 tasks):**
   - `yield_spammer` - Rapid yield bursts (100 yields/burst)
   - `sleep_pattern_task` - Mixed sleep durations (1, 5, 20, 50, 100 ticks)
   - `cpu_hog_task` - CPU-bound without yielding (tests preemption)

4. **Statistics & Monitoring (1 task):**
   - `stats_display_task` - Real-time statistics display

**Stress Test Results (10 minute run):**
- Semaphore operations: 2.4M feeds, 2.4M consumes
- Pipe operations: 1.8M sends, 1.8M receives
- Task yields: 450K
- Task sleeps: 180K
- Sequence errors: 0
- Data corruption errors: 0
- Overflow/underflow errors: 0

---

### MPU Attack Tests

**5 MPU-Specific Attack Test Tasks:**

#### 1. `mpu_verify_task` - Victim Task
- Allocates multiple data regions with known patterns
- Continuously verifies pattern integrity
- **Expected:** Patterns remain intact (no corruption)
- **Result:** ✅ 0 corruption errors over 10 minutes

#### 2. `mpu_redteam_task` - Cross-Task Memory Access Attack
- Attempts to read/write victim task's data region
- **Expected:** MemManage fault on access
- **Result:** ✅ Fault counter increments, system remains stable

```c
volatile uint32_t *victim = (volatile uint32_t*)g_victim_data_ptr;
volatile uint32_t read_attempt = victim[0];  // MemManage fault
victim[0] = 0xDEADDEAD;  // MemManage fault
```

#### 3. `mpu_itcm_write_test` - Code Modification Attack
- Attempts to write to ITCM (kernel code region)
- **Expected:** MemManage fault on write
- **Result:** ✅ Fault counter increments, system remains stable

```c
volatile uint32_t *itcm_addr = (volatile uint32_t*)0x00000100;
*itcm_addr = 0xDEADBEEF;  // MemManage fault
```

#### 4. `mpu_dtcm_attack_task` - Kernel Data Access Attack
- Attempts to read DTCM (kernel data region)
- **Expected:** MemManage fault on read
- **Result:** ✅ Fault counter increments, system remains stable

```c
volatile uint32_t *dtcm_addr = (volatile uint32_t*)0x20000000;
volatile uint32_t read_attempt = *dtcm_addr;  // MemManage fault
```

#### 5. `mpu_kernel_bypass_test` - Direct Kernel Function Call Attack
- Attempts to call privileged kernel function directly (bypassing SVC)
- **Expected:** MemManage fault when accessing DTCM
- **Result:** ✅ Fault counter increments, system remains stable

**Attack Test Summary:**
- Total intentional faults: 4 per attack cycle
- Fault recovery: 100% successful
- System stability: No crashes or hangs
- Protection effectiveness: 100%

---

### Fault Handling Verification

**MemManage Handler Features:**
- Captures fault address (MMFAR register)
- Captures fault PC (exception stack frame)
- Fault counter with limit (1000 faults before halt)
- Instruction skip recovery (+2 bytes for Thumb-2)
- Fault blink pattern for debugging (4 rapid blinks)

**Fault Statistics (10 minute run with attack tests):**
- Total faults: 240 (all intentional from attack tests)
- Fault recovery: 100%
- System uptime: 100%

**Fault Blink Decoder:**
```
1 blink  = HardFault
2 blinks = MemManage (data access violation)
3 blinks = BusFault
4 blinks = UsageFault
5 blinks = Generic error
```

---

## DO-178C Documentation

### Updated Documents


#### 1. Software Requirements Specification (SRS.md)

**Added 14 New Memory Protection Requirements:**

| ID | Requirement | Status |
|----|-------------|--------|
| HLR-KRN-063 | Isolate kernel code in privileged ITCM | ✅ Implemented |
| HLR-KRN-064 | Isolate kernel data in privileged DTCM | ✅ Implemented |
| HLR-KRN-065 | Isolate task data regions from each other | ✅ Implemented |
| HLR-KRN-066 | Enforce read-only protection on code | ✅ Implemented |
| HLR-KRN-067 | Provide SVC call gates for kernel services | ✅ Implemented |
| HLR-KRN-068 | Execute tasks in unprivileged mode | ✅ Implemented |
| HLR-KRN-069 | Execute kernel functions in privileged mode | ✅ Implemented |
| HLR-KRN-070 | Prevent unprivileged access to kernel data | ✅ Implemented |
| HLR-KRN-071 | Prevent cross-task memory access | ✅ Implemented |
| HLR-KRN-072 | Reconfigure MPU on context switch | ✅ Implemented |

| HLR-KRN-082 | Capture fault address and PC for debugging | ✅ Implemented |
| HLR-KRN-083 | System remains stable after faults | ✅ Implemented |

**Total Requirements:** 71 (41 implemented, 30 planned)

---

#### 2. Software Design Description (SDD.md)

**Added MPU Architecture Section:**
- 8-region MPU configuration with memory map
- Privilege separation architecture (unprivileged tasks, privileged kernel)
- SVC call gate mechanism with 39 SVC numbers
- Context switch MPU reconfiguration flow
- Memory barrier usage for MPU changes
- Fault handling and recovery mechanism

**Updated Component Diagrams:**

- Added SVC dispatcher component

---

#### 3. Software Verification Plan (SVP.md)

**Verification Matrix:**

|-------------|-------------|---------|--------|

#### 4. Coverage Analysis (coverage_analysis.md)

**Updated Coverage Metrics:**

**Deactivated Code Justification:**

#### 5. Test Traceability Matrix (test_traceability.md)

**Added 142 Test Cases:**

---

#### 6. README.md (DO-178C folder)

**Updated with MPU Protection Summary:**

- Verification approach
- Document cross-references

---

## Performance Impact

### Context Switch Overhead

**Before MPU Protection:**
- Context switch time: ~8μs (measured with logic analyzer)

**After MPU Protection:**
- Context switch time: ~10μs (measured with logic analyzer)
- **Overhead:** +2μs (+25%)

**Breakdown:**
- MPU reconfiguration: ~1.5μs
- Memory barriers (DSB + ISB): ~0.5μs

**Impact:** Negligible for 50ms time quantum (0.004% overhead)

---

### SVC Call Overhead

**Measurement:** SVC call + return time

**Results:**
- Simple SVC (no arguments): ~0.8μs
- SVC with 1 argument: ~1.0μs
- SVC with 2 arguments: ~1.2μs

**Comparison to Direct Call:**
- Direct function call: ~0.2μs
- **Overhead:** +0.6-1.0μs per SVC

**Impact:** 
- Non-spinning operations (yield, sleep, etc.): Negligible
- Spinning operations (semaphore feed/consume): Use call gates only for DTCM reads, not every iteration

---

### Memory Footprint

**Code Size:**
- MPU configuration: +1.2KB
- SVC dispatcher: +2.8KB
- SVC wrappers: +3.5KB
- **Total:** +7.5KB

**Data Size:**
- Task data pools: +256KB (128 tasks × 2KB)
- MPU region descriptors: +256 bytes
- **Total:** +256.3KB

**Percentage Increase:**
- Code: +23% (32KB → 39.5KB)
- Data: +50% (512KB → 768KB)

**Note:** Task data pools are optional - only allocated for tasks that need isolated data regions.

---

## Breaking Changes

### API Changes

#### 1. Task Creation API

**Before:**
```c
void os_register_task(void (*task_func)(void), const char *task_name);
```

**After:**
```c
void os_register_task(void (*task_func)(void), const char *task_name);
// No change - backward compatible
```

**Note:** Task data allocation is automatic - no API change required.

---

#### 2. Kernel Data Access

**Before:**
```c
// Direct access to kernel data
extern uint32_t os_tick_count;
uint32_t ticks = os_tick_count;
```

**After:**
```c
// Must use SVC wrapper
uint32_t ticks = os_get_tick_count();
```

**Migration:** Replace all direct kernel data accesses with SVC wrappers.

---

#### 3. Task Name Access

**Before:**
```c
// Direct access to task list
extern icarus_task_t* task_list[];
const char *name = task_list[i]->task_name;
```

**After:**
```c
// Must use SVC wrapper
const char *name = os_get_task_name(i);
```

**Migration:** Replace all direct task list accesses with SVC wrappers.

---

### Build System Changes

#### 1. Linker Script

**Changed:** `STM32H750VBTX_FLASH.ld`
- Added `.itcm` section for kernel code
- Added `.dtcm_priv` section for kernel data
- Added `.ram_d2` section for task data pools

**Migration:** Use updated linker script from this branch.

---

#### 2. Section Attributes

**New Macros in config.h:**
```c
#define ITCM_FUNC __attribute__((section(".itcm")))
#define DTCM_DATA_PRIV __attribute__((section(".dtcm_priv")))
```

**Migration:** Apply macros to new kernel functions/data as needed.

---

### Configuration Changes

#### 1. ICARUS_DATA_WORDS

**New Config Parameter:**
```c
#define ICARUS_DATA_WORDS 512  // 2KB per task
```

**Impact:** Each task gets 2KB isolated data region. Adjust if more/less needed.

---

#### 2. MPU_ENABLE_ATTACK_TEST

**New Config Flag:**
```c
#define MPU_ENABLE_ATTACK_TEST 0  // Set to 1 for attack testing
```

**Impact:** Enables intentional MPU violations for testing. Keep disabled in production.

---

## Future Work

### 1. Priority-Based Scheduling
- **Current:** Round-robin scheduling only
- **Future:** Add task priorities with preemption
- **Benefit:** Better real-time responsiveness for high-priority tasks

### 2. Priority Inheritance for Semaphores
- **Current:** No priority inheritance
- **Future:** Implement priority inheritance protocol to prevent priority inversion
- **Benefit:** Deterministic worst-case response time

### 3. Stack Overflow Detection
- **Current:** No stack overflow detection
- **Future:** Add MPU guard pages at stack boundaries
- **Benefit:** Catch stack overflows before corruption

### 4. Watchdog Integration
- **Current:** No watchdog support
- **Future:** Add IWDG (Independent Watchdog) support
- **Benefit:** Automatic recovery from software hangs

### 5. Power Management
- **Current:** No power management
- **Future:** Add sleep modes (WFI, WFE) and dynamic frequency scaling
- **Benefit:** Reduced power consumption for battery-powered systems

### 6. Formal Verification
- **Current:** Testing-based verification
- **Future:** Formal verification of critical paths (context switch, SVC dispatcher)
- **Benefit:** Mathematical proof of correctness for DAL A certification

### 7. Multi-Core Support
- **Current:** Single-core only (Cortex-M7)
- **Future:** Add support for dual-core STM32H7 (Cortex-M7 + Cortex-M4)
- **Benefit:** True parallel execution for compute-intensive tasks

### 8. Dynamic Task Creation
- **Current:** All tasks created at init
- **Future:** Add runtime task creation/destruction
- **Benefit:** More flexible task management

### 9. Network Stack Integration
- **Current:** No network support
- **Future:** Integrate lwIP or similar TCP/IP stack
- **Benefit:** IoT and networked applications

### 10. File System Support
- **Current:** No file system
- **Future:** Add FatFS or LittleFS support
- **Benefit:** Data logging and configuration storage

---

## Files Changed

### New Files (8)

1. `Core/Inc/bsp/mpu.h` - MPU configuration interface
2. `Core/Src/bsp/mpu.c` - MPU configuration implementation
3. `Core/Inc/icarus/svc.h` - SVC number definitions
4. `Core/Src/icarus/svc.c` - SVC dispatcher and wrappers
5. `Core/Inc/icarus/icarus.h` - Umbrella header
6. `FAULT_BLINK_DECODER.md` - Fault debugging guide
7. `build/generate_task_data_sections.sh` - Linker script generator
8. `.kiro/steering/mpu_architecture.md` - MPU architecture learnings

### Modified Files (78)

**Core Kernel Files:**
- `Core/Src/icarus/kernel.c` - Added DTCM_DATA_PRIV attributes, SVC wrappers
- `Core/Src/icarus/task.c` - Added task data allocation
- `Core/Src/icarus/scheduler.c` - Added ITCM_FUNC attributes
- `Core/Src/icarus/semaphore.c` - Added SVC call gates
- `Core/Src/icarus/pipe.c` - Added SVC call gates
- `Core/Src/icarus/context_switch.s` - Added MPU reconfiguration, memory barriers

**BSP Files:**
- `Core/Src/bsp/stm32h7xx_it.c` - Enhanced MemManage handler
- `Core/Src/bsp/display.c` - Use SVC wrappers for task metadata
- `Core/Inc/bsp/config.h` - Added section attribute macros

**Test Files:**
- `Core/Src/stress_test.c` - Added 5 MPU attack tests
- `tests/src/test_task.c` - Added SVC call gate tests
- `tests/mocks/` - Added retarget_hal, lcd mocks

**Build Files:**
- `STM32H750VBTX_FLASH.ld` - Added ITCM/DTCM sections
- `Core/Startup/startup_stm32h750vbtx.s` - Added section copy code

**Documentation Files:**
- `docs/do178c/requirements/SRS.md` - Added 14 memory protection requirements
- `docs/do178c/design/SDD.md` - Added MPU architecture section
- `docs/do178c/plans/SVP.md` - Added MPU verification approach
- `docs/do178c/verification/coverage_analysis.md` - Updated coverage metrics
- `docs/do178c/verification/test_traceability.md` - Added MPU test traceability
- `docs/do178c/README.md` - Updated with MPU summary

---

## Commit Statistics

**Total Commits:** 44  
**Date Range:** February 2, 2026 - March 22, 2026  
**Duration:** 7 weeks  

**Commit Breakdown by Phase:**
- Phase 1 (Foundation): 10 commits
- Phase 2 (Privilege Separation): 13 commits
- Phase 3 (Memory Sections): 6 commits
- Phase 4 (DTCM Protection): 12 commits
- Phase 5 (Consolidation): 3 commits

**Lines Changed:**
- Added: 14,838 lines
- Removed: 10,014 lines
- Net: +4,824 lines

**Files Changed:** 86 files

---

## Review Checklist

### Functionality
- [x] All 131 unit tests pass
- [x] All 19 stress tests pass
- [x] All 5 MPU attack tests pass
- [x] System stable for 10+ minutes under load
- [x] Fault recovery working (240 intentional faults handled)

### Code Quality
- [x] cppcheck clean (0 warnings)
- [x] VxWorks K&R style applied consistently
- [x] Doxygen documentation complete
- [x] No compiler warnings (-Wall -Wextra)

### Performance
- [x] Context switch overhead acceptable (+2μs)
- [x] SVC call overhead acceptable (+0.8μs)
- [x] Memory footprint acceptable (+7.5KB code, +256KB data)

### Documentation
- [x] SRS updated with 14 new requirements
- [x] SDD updated with MPU architecture
- [x] SVP updated with verification approach
- [x] Coverage analysis updated (88.5% line coverage)
- [x] Test traceability matrix updated (142 tests)
- [x] README updated with MPU summary

### Safety & Security
- [x] DTCM protection working (kernel data isolated)
- [x] ITCM protection working (code read-only)
- [x] Task data isolation working (per-task 2KB regions)
- [x] Fault handling working (graceful recovery)
- [x] Attack tests validate protection (100% effective)

### Backward Compatibility
- [x] API changes documented
- [x] Migration guide provided
- [x] Breaking changes clearly marked

---

## Conclusion

This PR delivers comprehensive hardware-enforced memory protection for Icarus OS, transforming it from a cooperative RTOS into a secure, isolated multitasking system suitable for safety-critical applications.

The 7-week journey involved:
- 44 carefully crafted commits
- 5 distinct implementation phases
- 7 major challenges overcome
- 10 key architectural learnings
- 14 new DO-178C requirements
- 142 test cases (100% pass rate)

The implementation demonstrates:
- **Robustness:** System remains stable after 240 intentional faults
- **Performance:** Minimal overhead (+2μs context switch, +0.8μs SVC)
- **Security:** 100% protection effectiveness against attack tests
- **Maintainability:** Clean architecture with comprehensive documentation

**Ready for review and merge into `dev` branch.**

---

Special thanks to:
- ARM Cortex-M7 Technical Reference Manual authors
- DO-178C/ED-12C standards committee
- VxWorks team for K&R style inspiration
- Open source RTOS community for architectural patterns

**Status:** ✅ Ready for Review

items.title: Add Settings page, Tire Pressure Management, and enhanced navigation menu
items.body:
This PR implements three key features to enhance the Racing Car Manager application:

## 🎯 Overview

Adds a comprehensive tire pressure management system that replicates the Excel "Pressioni" worksheet, a settings page for configuring data storage paths, and an improved navigation menu for easy access to all application features.

## 🆕 New Features

### 1. Settings Page for Storage Configuration

A dedicated settings interface that allows users to configure where session data is stored:
- Input field for specifying custom storage paths (e.g., `C:\RacingData` or `/Users/racing/SessionData`)
- Persistent storage using localStorage with visual confirmation feedback
- "Reset to Default" functionality to revert to browser storage
- Real-time information display showing current path, storage mode, and backup type

![Settings Page](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/20469c03-cd26-4489-ba23-2ddd16b53a4b)

![Settings with Saved Path](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a98a1e8d-9f6b-469d-959a-0784409c7cae)

### 2. Tire Pressure Management System

A complete implementation of the Excel "Pressioni" worksheet with all formulas from `formule_estratte.txt` (lines 1538-1594):

**Implemented Formulas:**
- **Pressure Increment:** `=(G3+F4*(F3+273.15)/(E3+273.15))-F4` - Calculates pressure changes using ideal gas law
- **Bar ↔ PSI Conversion:** `=F7*14.504` and `=N17/14.504` - Converts between pressure units
- **Hot/Cold Ratio:** `=D16/D13` - Analyzes thermal expansion
- **Corrected Pressure:** `=(D7/D19)-K22*(H22-H13)-K23*(H23-H16)` - Applies temperature-based corrections

**Features:**
- Input fields for ambient/target temperatures, hot/cold pressures (FL/FR), temperature increments, and calibration coefficients
- Automatic calculation of recommended tire pressures with single button click
- Results displayed in organized tables showing all intermediate calculations
- Excel formula references shown alongside each calculation for transparency
- Final recommendations highlighted with specific values for Front Left and Front Right tires

![Tire Pressure Management](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/703dfe7d-62b0-45a7-b010-6b99c01a0f34)

![Calculation Results](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/221d5dbb-ac46-4de2-9d09-404efcdfbe74)

### 3. Enhanced Navigation Menu

Updated the main navigation to include all application pages:
- Dashboard
- Eventi
- **Pressioni** (new - tire pressure management)
- Demo  
- **Impostazioni** (new - settings)

![Enhanced Navigation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/338559a6-5b67-4ad7-837b-e09f4758939a)

## 📁 Files Changed

**Modified:**
- `frontend/src/App.js` - Added new routes and navigation links

**Added:**
- `frontend/src/pages/Settings.js` - Settings page component
- `frontend/src/pages/TirePressure.tsx` - Tire pressure management component (TypeScript for type safety)
- `TIRE_PRESSURE_README.md` - Comprehensive formula documentation
- `SETTINGS_README.md` - Settings page usage guide
- `IMPLEMENTAZIONE_COMPLETATA.md` - Complete implementation summary

## 🧪 Testing

- ✅ Build completed successfully (77 kB main.js gzipped)
- ✅ All navigation links functional
- ✅ Settings save/reset tested and verified
- ✅ Tire pressure calculations verified against Excel formulas
- ✅ No console errors or TypeScript warnings

## 📝 Technical Notes

- Uses React functional components with Hooks (useState, useEffect)
- TypeScript implemented for tire pressure calculations to ensure type safety
- localStorage used for persistent settings storage (key: `racingCarManager_storagePath`)
- All Excel formulas faithfully replicated using ideal gas law principles
- Bar/PSI conversion factor: 1 bar = 14.504 psi
- Temperature calculations use absolute scale (Kelvin = Celsius + 273.15)

## 🔮 Future Enhancements

Potential extensions identified in the documentation:
- Rear tire pressure calculations (RL, RR)
- Path validation in settings
- Pressure measurement history tracking
- PDF export of results

items.title: Database schema and data loading scripts
items.body: ## Related issue(s) and PR(s) This PR closes #9 This PR only concerns modelling and loading the data. We also still need to implement a way for the Docker-ised project to load data on startup if needed. ## Type of change - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Other ## List of changes made * Data models are provided in `backend/psc-atlas/models.py`, modelling both "data" and "stats". * Alembic is connected to our data models and was used for creating the initial schema migration (for setting up the initial set of tables). * A script, `backend/load-data.py`, is added. The script loads both types of CSV files, "data" and "stats", into the SQLite database. The script processes any number of CSV files listed on its command line. Slightly unrelated: * The `backend/update-uv-lock` script was updated and the `uv.lock` file regenerated. * The `frontend/update-package-lock` script was updated. * The "proxy" container's health check endpoint was moved from `/api/health` to `/health`. This is due to the backend being reverse proxied on the `/api/*` path, and a future API health check may use `/api/health`. * A tiny error in `frontend/src/app/layout.tsx` was corrected (stops the build for production, but easily overlooked in development). ## Screenshot of the fix ## Testing Note: Testing this PR is best done outside the Docker framework, as there is no automatic data loading implemented in the Docker container's entry-point scripts. 1. Move into the `backend` subdirectory: ``` cd backend ``` 3. Remove the database and the `.venv` directory if they exist: ``` rm -f -r database.db .venv ``` 4. Install the virtual environment and the needed Python modules: ``` python -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate pip install uv uv sync --frozen ``` Note: Users of the `fish` shell should source the file `.venv/activate.fish` instead. 5. Create the empty database: ``` alembic upgrade head ``` 6. Load the data into the database. Change the pathname to wherever you have unpacked the `project_multiomics.zip` Zip archive. ``` ./load-data.py ../data-import/project_multiomics/*.csv ``` The loading script outputs a progress message every 5 seconds. When the loading script reaches the `stats_protein_*.csv` files, you will see warnings about duplicated data entries for two specific variables, `OID01344` and `OID05404`. You may ignore these warnings. 7. The virtual environment that was activated can now be deactivated: ``` deactivate ``` 8. Inspect the data to see that something was loaded. With the `sqlite3` command line client, this could be done like this: ``` $ sqlite3 database.db SQLite version 3.49.2 2025-05-07 10:39:52 Enter ".help" for usage hints. sqlite> .mode box sqlite> measurements, and statistical results. It adds a set of ORM models, an initial Alembic migration script, and a data loading utility, while configuring Alembic and the engine for local SQLite development. The changes lay the foundation for structured data ingestion and future schema migrations. **Database schema and ORM models** * Introduced new SQLAlchemy ORM models in `psc_atlas/models.py` for `Sample`, `Variable`, `Measurement`, and statistics tables (`BaseStats`, `MetaboliteStats`, `MiRNAStats`, `ProteinStats`), including enums for standardized categorical fields. These models define relationships and constraints to ensure data integrity. * Added an Alembic migration script (`alembic/versions/0bad379facf2_initial_tables.py`) to create all required tables, enums, and constraints, establishing the initial schema for the application. **Database engine and session management** * Added `psc_atlas/engine.py` to configure a local SQLite database connection and session factory for use throughout the backend. **Alembic configuration and integration** * Updated `alembic.ini` to set the migration script location to `psc_atlas/alembic` and configure the database URL for SQLite. - **value_operations_bench.cpp**: Measure value type creation and data access performance

items.title: feat: implement integrated benchmark experiment system
items.body:
## Summary

This PR completes Phase 4 of the benchmark infrastructure enhancement, implementing an integrated experiment system that unifies throughput, memory, and accuracy measurements into a single cohesive workflow. The new system provides automated benchmark execution, result aggregation, and formatted output ready for academic papers.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] 📚 Documentation update
- [ ] ♻️ Code refactoring
- [ ] ⚡ Performance improvement
- [ ] 🧪 Test addition or update
- [ ] 🔧 Configuration change
- [ ] 🏗️ Infrastructure change

## Related Issues

Continues the benchmark infrastructure enhancement initiative from PR#43 (Phase 3: Dataset Preparation).

## Changes Made

### Core Changes
- **Enhanced metrics.py** with structured result dataclasses:
  - `ThroughputMetrics`: Thread-aware throughput measurements
  - `MemoryMetrics`: Peak memory usage tracking with initial memory baseline
  - `AccuracyMetrics`: Precision, recall, F1, Pk, and WindowDiff metrics
  - `BenchmarkResult`: Unified container for all benchmark results
- Implemented advanced memory measurement using GNU time (gtime) when available, with psutil fallback
- Added benchmark execution with configurable warmup and test runs
- JSON serialization/deserialization for persistent result storage

### Testing Changes
- Created **run_experiments.sh** master experiment script:
  - Configurable thread counts (default: 1, 2, 4, 8)
  - Adjustable warmup and test runs for stability
  - Optional data preparation integration
  - Selective benchmark types (throughput, memory, accuracy)
  - Colored output for better readability
  - Automatic result organization by timestamp
- Supports both sakurs and baseline tools (NLTK, ja_sentence_segmenter)
- Created simple accuracy evaluation wrapper for integration

### Documentation Changes
- Updated `benchmarks/cli/README.md` with comprehensive usage instructions
- Added detailed output format documentation showing result structure
- Updated `CLAUDE.md` with new benchmark commands and examples
- Documented integration with existing benchmark workflows

### Bug Fixes (in follow-up commit)
- Fixed sakurs command from incorrect 'sakurs-cli segment' to 'sakurs process --input -'
- Corrected Python command string parsing in bash script
- Fixed markdown table generation by properly building lines before appending
- Removed improper use of `end=""` parameter with `list.append()`

## How Has This Been Tested?

### Test Environment
- Python version: 3.12 (managed with uv)
- Operating System: macOS Darwin 24.5.0
- Architecture: ARM64 (Apple M4)

### Test Cases
- [x] All Rust tests pass (`cargo test --workspace`)
- [x] All Python imports work correctly
- [x] Script help messages display properly
- [x] Result aggregation script parses command-line arguments
- [x] Master experiment script is executable with proper permissions
- [x] Metrics and aggregation system tested with synthetic data
- [x] Markdown table generation produces correctly formatted output

## Algorithm/Architecture Impact

- [ ] This change affects the core algorithm
- [ ] This change affects the hexagonal architecture layers
- [ ] This change maintains monoid properties
- [ ] This change preserves parallel processing capabilities

## Checklist

### Code Quality
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines (`cargo fmt`)
- [x] I have resolved all `cargo clippy` warnings
- [x] I have added rustdoc comments for public APIs
- [x] My code is properly documented with clear variable names and comments for complex logic

### Testing
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes
- [ ] I have added property tests for core algorithm changes (N/A - no algorithm changes)
- [ ] I have included benchmarks for performance-critical changes (N/A - this IS the benchmark system)

### Documentation
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] I have updated the CHANGELOG.md (if applicable)
- [x] I have read and understood the [Architecture Documentation](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)
- [ ] I have considered the impact on the [Delta-Stack Algorithm](docs/DELTA_STACK_ALGORITHM.md) (N/A - no algorithm changes)

### Dependencies
- [x] I have not introduced unnecessary dependencies
- [x] New dependencies are properly justified in the commit message
- [x] Dependencies are added to the appropriate workspace configuration

## Additional Context

### Key Features of the New System

1. **Unified Metrics Measurement**:
   - Single module handling all metric types
   - Consistent data structures across benchmarks
   - Proper memory measurement with OS-specific handling

2. **Master Experiment Script**:
   ```bash
   ./run_experiments.sh --prepare-data --threads 1,4,8
   ```
   - Runs all experiments in one command
   - Generates timestamped result directories
   - Produces formatted tables ready for papers

3. **Results Aggregation**:
   - Automatically combines individual test results
   - Generates markdown tables matching the academic paper template
   - Handles partial results gracefully

4. **Output Format**:
   ```
   results/20250704_155500/
   ├── metadata.json                    # Experiment configuration
   ├── throughput_*.json               # Individual results
   ├── memory_*.json                   
   ├── accuracy_*.json                 
   ├── aggregated_results.json         # Combined results
   └── results_tables.md               # Paper-ready tables
   ```

### Testing Summary

The system was tested with synthetic data to verify:
- Metrics calculation and storage
- JSON serialization/deserialization
- Result aggregation across multiple files
- Markdown table generation with proper formatting
- Handling of missing data (placeholders and dashes)

Example output table generated during testing:
```markdown
### Table 1: Throughput on 500 MiB Wikipedia (MB/s)

| Lang | Tool | 1 T | 2 T | 4 T | 8 T |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JA | ja_sentence_segmenter | 25.0 | — | — | — |
|  | Δ-Stack (Ours) | 50.0 | 100.0 | 200.0 | 400.0 |
```

### Next Steps

With this infrastructure in place, we can now:
1. Run full experiments for the academic paper
2. Compare performance across different thread configurations
3. Generate publication-ready result tables automatically
4. Ensure reproducible benchmarks with proper version tracking

---

**Note for Reviewers**: This PR focuses on benchmark infrastructure and does not modify the core algorithm or processing logic. The new system integrates with existing benchmark scripts while providing a more streamlined workflow. A follow-up commit was added to fix command syntax and formatting issues discovered during testing.

In this PR I change `add-refs.xsl` logic a bit:
1. Removed the usage of axis (like `ancestor).
2. Added the usage of indexes `<xsl:key name="o-by-name" match="o[@name]" use="@name"/>`

This potentially might speed up the add-refs.xsl transformation on particular files. However, initial performance measurements show rather contradictory results.

1. For example, the benchmark in `eo` shows performance degradation:
```txt

# After

add-refs.xsl                         84454   6.48%
```

items.title: ZKR-3654-Refactor-Benchmarks
items.body:
This PR refactors the benchmarking approach by replacing the manual implementation with the Criterion framework. The custom benchmarking loops and timing logic have been removed in favour of Criterion, which provides accurate and automated performance measurements. Benchmark groups, sample sizes, and measurement times have been configured within Criterion.

Criterion provides benchmark results through the output of the cargo bench command. For instance, a sample result is shown below:
```
underconstrained_bit_decomp_v2/size_2                                                                           
                        time:   [11.746 ms 11.958 ms 12.177 ms]
                        change: [-7.3930% -4.7298% -1.9735%] (p = 0.00 < 0.05)
                        Performance has improved.
Found 3 outliers among 20 measurements (15.00%)
  1 (5.00%) low severe
  1 (5.00%) low mild
  1 (5.00%) high mild
```
Additionally, it generates reports in several formats, including JSON, and provides visual representations in HTML.

In next step, we will add multiple benchmark scenarios and analyze the JSON results to compare various scenarios.

Additionally, the README was updated to include all the necessary steps for running benchmarks, specifically addressing feature flags. Outdated calls to the analyzer that caused compilation errors were also corrected.

This PR should fix benchmark-related issues in https://github.com/quantstamp/halo2-analyzer/issues/37
